exam_standard.reference: Osaka Prefectural Police: provisional license written test is 50 questions in 30 minutes; passing requires 90% or higher.

notes: A1 and B1 are the only public bank identifiers in this build.

questions.question_en: This pavement marking indicates that vehicles may not pass through the area of the marking.
questions.explanation: The depicted yellow-bordered road marking is a no-entry area (立入り禁止部分); vehicles must not enter the marked part.

questions.question_en: When approaching a pedestrian crossing, drivers may keep your speed without slowing down if it is clear that there is no pedestrian that is crossing.
questions.explanation: At a pedestrian crossing, you must slow enough to stop unless it is clearly evident that no pedestrian or bicycle is crossing or about to cross. If it is clearly empty, that slowdown duty does not apply.

questions.question_en: When stopping a vehicle, it is alright to brake strongly only once because hitting the brakes several times will disorient the vehicles behind.
questions.explanation: The NPA guide recommends braking progressively and, where appropriate, using the brake several times; flashing brake lamps can warn following traffic. Sudden hard braking is only for unavoidable danger.

questions.question_en: When proceeding to a road, make sure that other vehicles or pedestrians can safely proceed by following rules and keeping in mind the road and traffic rules.
questions.explanation: Drivers must follow traffic rules and pay attention to surrounding road users so that everyone can travel safely.

questions.question_en: If you took medications because of headaches or colds that may induce drowsiness, you must not drive.
questions.explanation: The NPA guide specifically says not to drive after taking cold or headache medicine that has a drowsiness effect.

questions.question_en: The traffic signal light ahead is flashing red, you may reduce speed and go through while paying attention on the intersecting road.
questions.explanation: A flashing red signal requires vehicles to stop at the stopping position before proceeding; merely slowing is insufficient.

questions.question_en: In general rules, vehicles should proceed through the left side of the center line if a center line is present.
questions.explanation: Vehicles generally must travel on the left side of the road center, or left of the center line when one is present, subject to listed exceptions.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that cars wider than 2.2 meters including their load may not proceed through.
questions.explanation: The sign is a maximum-width restriction. The vehicle including its load must not exceed the displayed width.

questions.question_en: When there is a child playing on the road, you can pass through without slowing down as long as you sound your horn.
questions.explanation: When a child may be in danger, drivers must stop or slow so the child can pass safely. The horn does not give a driver priority or replace the duty to protect the child.

questions.question_en: On a road with vehicular lanes, recklessly changing lanes disturbs the vehicles behind and may cause troubles.
questions.explanation: The NPA guide says drivers must not change lanes unnecessarily because doing so inconveniences following traffic and can cause crashes.

questions.question_en: If it is difficult to pass through the left of the center line due to road work, drivers may go into the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: When road works make the left portion insufficient for passage, a vehicle may use part of the right side, while minimizing the encroachment and ensuring safety.

questions.question_en: Automobiles and motorized bicycles should not go through pedestrian paths, side strips or bicycle lanes except when crossing to enter and exit areas that are adjacent to the road.
questions.explanation: Vehicles must not normally travel on sidewalks, roadside strips or bicycle paths, but may cross them to enter or leave roadside property, subject to safety duties.

questions.question_en: A driver of an automobile don't always need to follow the indicated arrows on roads with these markings even it's safe to do so.
questions.explanation: When directional lane markings designate how traffic must proceed at an intersection, drivers must follow the indicated direction except for narrow statutory exceptions such as yielding to an emergency vehicle or unavoidable road works.

questions.question_en: At an intersection with stop signs, it's permitted to stop briefly once, then proceed into the intersection before other vehicles crosses the intersection.
questions.explanation: A stop sign requires a full stop and the driver must not obstruct vehicles or trams using the intersecting road. Stopping first does not automatically give priority.

questions.question_en: When passing a bicycle and trying to turn left, you were about to encroach on the bicycle, you may sound the horn to warn the bicycle and turn left first.
questions.explanation: A driver turning left must avoid cutting across or endangering a bicycle. Sounding the horn does not create priority; the horn is limited to required horn locations or unavoidable danger.

questions.question_en: In a situation of violation and a police officer asked for your driving license, you don't need to show it.
questions.explanation: A driver must carry the appropriate licence and must present it when a police officer requests it after a traffic violation or accident.

questions.question_en: When approaching a railway crossing, lower your speed in advance to stop safely before the railway crossing (or right before the stop line if present).
questions.explanation: Before crossing a railway crossing, drivers must stop immediately before it or before the stop line and check safety, unless a traffic signal at the crossing permits passage. Slowing in advance so you can make that stop is correct.

questions.question_en: When the traffic light turns yellow, and you cannot stop safely as you were near the stop line, you went through.
questions.explanation: A yellow signal normally requires stopping, but if the signal changes to yellow when you are so close that you cannot stop safely, you may continue.

questions.question_en: A driver of a vehicle and motorized bicycle may use cellphones while driving and the flow of the traffic is light.
questions.explanation: Using a handheld cellphone for a call while driving is prohibited regardless of whether traffic is light, except when the vehicle is stopped or within the applicable automated-driving exception.

questions.explanation: The pictured blue rectangular arrow is a one-way indication; it does not mean the start of a traffic-regulation zone.

questions.question_en: In 30 meters in front of a pedestrian crossing, you may not change lane to pass another vehicle or motorized bicycles or go beside them.
questions.explanation: At a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing and within 30 m before it, a vehicle must not overtake or pass another vehicle so as to move ahead of it.

questions.question_en: When driving a regular vehicle going through a priority vehicle lane such as for fixed route bus lane, and a fixed route bus is approaching from behind, the driver may speed up and continue driving.
questions.explanation: A vehicle using a route-bus priority lane must promptly leave it when a route bus approaches, rather than speeding up and continuing in the lane.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第2節 自動車の通行するところ

questions.question_en: When passing closely a stopped vehicle, you need to anticipate that the vehicle door may suddenly open and proceed cautiously by passing at a reduced speed and maintain safety distance.
questions.explanation: Drivers should anticipate a suddenly opening door or a person emerging from behind a stopped vehicle and pass cautiously with appropriate clearance and speed.

sources.section: 第5章 第3節 歩行者の保護など

questions.question_en: While driving a vehicle and you lost track of your way, so you drove while focusing on the car navigation (excluding when driving an automated self-driving vehicle)
questions.explanation: A driver must not stare at a navigation display while driving because it reduces attention to surrounding traffic.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第4章 第5節 安全運転に必要な知識など (運転姿勢、携帯電話、シートベルト、チャイルドシート)

questions.question_en: In an intersection that this sign is posted, you should proceed after stopping once and not to block vehicles that are proceeding through the intersecting road.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, stop at the stopping position and do not obstruct traffic on the intersecting road.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第7節 交差点の通り方

questions.question_en: Drivers may use the horn adhering to ‘horn blowing’ and ‘horn area’ signs, and when it's necessary in order to avoid danger, but you should not sound horn in any other cases.
questions.explanation: The horn must be sounded where a “sound horn” sign or required horn-zone situation applies, and may be used when unavoidable to prevent danger; otherwise it must not be sounded.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第5節 進路変更など

questions.question_en: When driving not in the vicinity of or in an intersection, drivers should go to the left side of the road and yield when an emergency vehicle approaches from behind.
questions.explanation: Outside an intersection or its vicinity, drivers must move to the left side and yield the way to an approaching emergency vehicle (with the one-way-road exception where moving left would obstruct it).

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第2節 自動車の通行するところ

questions.question_en: When making a right turn in an intersection, it's easier and safer to turn staying on the left side of the road in advance.
questions.explanation: For a normal right turn, a driver should move as close as practicable to the road center in advance and turn slowly just inside the intersection center; staying at the left edge is not the standard method.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第7節 交差点の通り方

questions.question_en: When vehicle lanes dedicated to fixed route buses are marked on the left side of the road, drivers may not go through that dedicated vehicle lane even when making a left turn.
questions.explanation: Other vehicles are generally barred from a bus-only lane, but entering it as necessary to prepare for a left turn is an explicit exception.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第2節 自動車の通行するところ

questions.question_en: This pavement marking indicates an area that stopping is not permitted, drivers must not enter when there is a risk that the vehicle will be stuck in the area.
questions.explanation: A “no stopping area” marking is used where vehicles must not stop; if congestion could trap the vehicle in the marked area, it must not enter.

questions.question_en: Making sure to move into the open vehicle traffic lanes at all times on a road with vehicular lanes will make the traffic smoother and prevent risk.
questions.explanation: Drivers must not weave or change lanes unnecessarily. An open lane does not justify constant lane changes.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第2節 自動車の通行するところ

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第5節 進路変更など

questions.question_en: When passing through intersections drivers should proceed with a safe speed and method as possible while adequately pay attention for pedestrians and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At and around intersections, drivers must pay attention to pedestrians and other traffic and proceed using the safest speed and method appropriate to the situation.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第7節 交差点の通り方

questions.question_en: When approaching a pedestrian crossing, drivers should slow down and able to stop before it when it's not clear whether there are pedestrians crossing or not.
questions.explanation: Unless it is clearly evident that nobody is crossing or about to cross, drivers approaching a crosswalk must slow sufficiently to be able to stop before it.

questions.question_en: A person must not ask a person to drive if that person is drunk or does not have a license.
questions.explanation: The NPA guide says not to ask an unlicensed person or a person who has been drinking to drive.

questions.question_en: Vehicles that proceeds to this light may not cross the stop line and proceed.
questions.explanation: For a steady yellow signal, vehicles must not proceed beyond the stopping position. Exception: if the light changes to yellow when the vehicle is already too close to stop safely, it may continue.
notes: The source sentence omits the official yellow-signal exception; the answer treats it as the normal meaning of a steady yellow signal.

questions.question_en: When driving in a corner of the road, driver should drive in a reduced speed.
questions.explanation: Drivers must proceed at a reduced speed near road bends/corners.

questions.question_en: When making a left turn, proceed with a reduced speed while staying as far left as possible in advance, adhering to the side of the intersection.
questions.explanation: For a left turn, move as close as practicable to the left edge in advance and proceed slowly along the edge of the intersection.

sources.section: 第5章 第7節 交差点の通り方

questions.question_en: Before starting an automatic vehicle, verify that the gear shift is in D position before stepping on the brake pedal and start the engine.
questions.explanation: Before starting an automatic vehicle, confirm the parking brake is applied and the selector is in P, then press the brake pedal and start the engine. D is selected for moving forward after starting.

questions.question_en: Cars that proceeds towards this light may turn right at the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green right-arrow signal permits vehicles to proceed in the arrow direction even when the main signal is red or yellow, subject to the special rules for certain light vehicles/mopeds.

questions.question_en: Correctly using a child seat may reduce damage from potential traffic accidents and prevent the child obstructing the driver.
questions.explanation: Correct use of a child seat substantially reduces injury in a crash and helps prevent a child from interfering with driving controls.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates one way street, drivers may not proceed in the opposite direction of the arrow.

questions.question_en: When passing by pedestrians you should slow down even if there is a safety distance between your vehicle and the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: When passing a pedestrian, the rule is to keep a safe lateral distance OR travel at reduced speed. If a sufficient safe distance is maintained, slowing is not automatically required.

questions.question_en: Vehicles must proceed through the left side of the center lines of the road when a center line is present.
questions.explanation: Vehicles generally must travel on the left side of the road center/center line, subject to statutory exceptions.

questions.question_en: If a driver of an automobile is driving leaning to one side, it's not dangerous as long as it's easier to drive that way
questions.explanation: The NPA guide instructs drivers to maintain a proper driving posture and specifically says not to drive with the body leaning diagonally.

questions.question_en: Vehicles may not pass through on roads that this sign is posted, but motorized bicycles may.
questions.explanation: The pictured sign is “No vehicles” (車両通行止め). It prohibits vehicles generally, which includes general motorized bicycles/mopeds; they are not exempt.

questions.question_en: While driving back from work, urgent call came and you picked up your phone to make conversation.
questions.explanation: Holding and using a cellphone for a call while driving is prohibited even when the call is urgent; stop safely before using it.

questions.question_en: I general rule, when passing automobiles and mopeds, drivers should pass on the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: As a general overtaking rule, pass another vehicle on its right. Exceptions apply, such as when the vehicle ahead is positioned to turn right or when passing a tram.

questions.question_en: When passing by pedestrians, you should keep a safety distance between the vehicle and the pedestrians or drive with a reduced speed.
questions.explanation: The NPA guide expressly requires either a safe separation from pedestrians or reduced speed.

questions.question_en: Hitting the brakes several times will disorient the vehicles behind, so when stopping it's fine to brake strongly once.
questions.explanation: Using the brakes progressively and, where appropriate, in several applications can warn following traffic. Sudden hard braking should be avoided except for unavoidable danger.

questions.question_en: When being passed by another vehicle and there is no enough space to pass, you should stay to the left as much as possible.
questions.explanation: A vehicle being overtaken must not increase speed and, where there is insufficient room, must move as far left as practicable to allow the overtaking vehicle to pass.

questions.explanation: The sign prohibits crossing into the right-hand portion of the road for the purpose of overtaking.

questions.explanation: Overtaking a vehicle that is itself overtaking another automobile is prohibited (double overtaking); staying below the speed limit does not make it legal.

questions.question_en: When passing by a mud or puddles, the driver is not responsible for splashing muddy water on pedestrians as long as the vehicle drives at a reduced speed.
questions.explanation: Drivers must take care not to splash mud or water on others, using reduced speed or other precautions. Driving slowly does not remove responsibility if you still splash them.

questions.question_en: In the image of this marking, vehicles that pass through vehicle traffic lane B may change their lane to vehicle traffic lane A.
questions.explanation: A yellow lane-boundary line prohibits crossing it for a lane change from the side where the yellow line applies. In the depicted arrangement, lane B is on the yellow-line side, so B-to-A is prohibited.
notes: The photographed diagram uses a paired white/yellow lane boundary; answer is based on the yellow line being on lane B side.

questions.question_en: When the traffic signal light ahead turns to yellow and you weren't able to stop safely as you were approaching the stop line, you went through.

questions.question_en: When a route bus signals to take off from the bus stop, vehicles behind should avoid that take off, excluding when they would have to brake suddenly.
questions.explanation: A following vehicle must not obstruct a route bus that has signaled to leave a stop, except when avoiding the bus would require sudden braking or steering.

questions.explanation: With three or more lanes in one direction, the rightmost lane should generally be kept for overtaking; slower traffic uses the left, with faster traffic progressively to the right. Posted lane-use rules take precedence.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第2節 自動車の通行するところ

questions.question_en: When the vehicle ahead is trying to pass another vehicle, as the driver you should drive safely and take responsibility.
questions.explanation: As written, this is a general safety statement: every driver remains responsible for safe driving. It does not authorize a second overtake; double overtaking remains prohibited.
notes: The English source is unusually vague and does not state a specific manoeuvre. The answer is limited to the literal wording; do not interpret it as permission to overtake.

questions.question_en: Using a child seat correctly may reduce damage from heavy traffic accidents and prevent obstructing the driver.
questions.explanation: A correctly fitted child seat reduces crash injury and helps prevent the child from interfering with driving.

questions.question_en: When an emergency vehicle is approaching from behind, and driving not in a vicinity on a road other than intersection, you should go to the lefthand side of the road and yield.
questions.explanation: Outside an intersection or its vicinity, move to the left and yield the way to the emergency vehicle, unless on a one-way road where moving left would obstruct it.

questions.question_en: When driving a motorized bicycle or mopeds, if there is no speed limit designated by signs or markings you may drive up to a speed of 30km/h.
questions.explanation: The general maximum speed for a general motorized bicycle/moped is 30 km/h; if a lower maximum is posted, the lower limit applies.

questions.question_en: Vehicles that comes to this traffic signal light may proceed through while paying attention to other traffic.
questions.explanation: The pictured flashing yellow signal allows vehicles to proceed while paying attention to other traffic.

questions.question_en: If it is difficult to pass through the left side of the center line of the road due to construction, drivers may proceed into the right side to pass.
questions.explanation: Road works that make the left portion insufficient are an explicit exception permitting limited use of the right side, provided it is done safely and with minimal encroachment.

sources.section: 第5章 第2節 自動車の通行するところ

questions.question_en: When your traffic signal is flashing yellow in an intersection, you should make sure to stop.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow signal means proceed with caution; it does not require a stop. A flashing red signal requires stopping.

questions.explanation: The depicted pavement symbol is the U-turn-prohibited marking (転回禁止). The source English uses “turning,” but the official meaning is specifically that a U-turn/turning around is prohibited, not that every left or right turn is prohibited.
notes: Translation note: “turning” is imprecise; the official marking means U-turn prohibited (転回禁止).

questions.explanation: A vehicle in a route-bus priority lane must promptly leave the lane when a route bus approaches from behind.

questions.question_en: While driving back at work, you remember an urgent business, so you picked up your cell phone to make a call while driving. (excluding cases when using automated self-driving vehicle)
questions.explanation: Using a handheld cellphone for a call while driving is prohibited, apart from the limited automated-driving exception specified by law; urgency of the call is not an exception.

questions.question_en: When starting a vehicle, you don't need to use your turn signal as long as you check vehicles coming from behind with your side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before starting from the roadside, signal your intention to start and then confirm safety again using mirrors and direct observation. Checking mirrors does not replace the signal.

questions.question_en: When driving through an intersection with poor visibility to the left and right, you should slow down even if the road you are passing through has the right of way.
questions.explanation: Drivers must slow at a blind intersection except where traffic is signal-controlled or when traveling on a priority road. Therefore “even if the road has the right of way” is not the legal rule.

questions.question_en: When going through intersections, drivers must immediately stop when an emergency vehicle approaches.
questions.explanation: Near an intersection, a driver should avoid entering/clear the intersection, move to the left and stop. Stopping immediately inside the intersection can obstruct the emergency vehicle and is not the rule.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第2節 自動車の通行するところ

questions.question_en: A driver should keep a safety distance between cars considering the weather, tire conditions, road surface and cargo weight so that you won't collide into the vehicle in front of you even the vehicle ahead stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Safe following distance must account for weather, road and tire condition, load and other factors so that you can avoid colliding even if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

sources.section: 第5章 第4節 安全な速度と車間距離

questions.question_en: When driving a standard vehicle and going through a priority lane such as for fixed-route buses, a fixed route bus had approach from behind, so you speed up and continued driving in the priority vehicle lane.
questions.explanation: When a route bus approaches from behind in a priority lane, an ordinary vehicle must promptly leave the lane rather than speed up and continue.

sources.section: 第5章 第2節 自動車の通行するところ

questions.question_en: In an intersection where traffic is not regulated (excluding roundabouts), when the crossing road is a priority lane or is wider, drive at reduced speed and yield to vehicles that are going through the intersecting road.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, if the intersecting road is a priority road or clearly wider, slow down and do not obstruct vehicles or trams on that road.

sources.title: 交通の方法に関する教則
sources.section: 第5章 第7節 交差点の通り方

questions.question_en: When nearing or approaching a pedestrian crossing, drivers should slow down so that you are able to stop at any time before it when it's not clear whether there are pedestrians or not in the pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Unless it is clearly evident that nobody is crossing or about to cross, slow sufficiently to stop before the crosswalk.

questions.explanation: Drivers must obey the signal facing them. A side-direction red signal does not guarantee that your signal is green because all-red periods and time-offset signals exist.

questions.explanation: A maximum-height sign applies to the total vehicle height including the load. If the vehicle plus cargo exceeds 3.3 m, it may not pass.

questions.question_en: With a three-point seat belts, it's advisable to make sure to tighten the shoulder belt so that it lies flat and avoids the neck in pain.
questions.explanation: A three-point belt should be snug, not twisted or slack, with the shoulder belt positioned so it does not run over the neck.

questions.question_en: When passing through a railroad crossing, drivers need not to stop right before it (or before the stop line if there is one) as long as an alarm isn't ringing.
questions.explanation: Drivers must stop immediately before a railway crossing or its stop line and check both directions, unless a traffic signal at the crossing permits passage. The absence of an alarm does not remove the stop requirement.

sources.section: 第6章 第1節 踏切

questions.question_en: In cases when you drink at night and still under the influence of alcohol the following morning of driving, you need to be vigilant.
questions.explanation: True. The National Police Agency teaching guide specifically warns that alcohol consumed the previous night may still affect a driver the following morning, so drivers must be vigilant about this carry-over effect. If alcohol is still affecting you, you must not drive.
notes: Answer-sheet cross-check: marked TRUE. The English wording is awkward; it corresponds to the NPA warning that alcohol from the previous night may still affect next-morning driving.

questions.explanation: Directional lane markings must be followed. Emergency-vehicle yielding and unavoidable road works are recognized exceptions.

questions.explanation: A “no stopping area” in front of police/fire facilities must be kept clear. You must not enter it when congestion could cause you to stop there; the rule is not suspended merely because no emergency dispatch is occurring.

questions.explanation: A standard/ordinary motor-vehicle licence permits ordinary cars, small special vehicles and general motorized bicycles, but not standard motorcycles; a motorcycle licence is required for those.

questions.question_en: When closely passing by a stopped vehicle, drivers need to anticipate that the door may suddenly open and proceed with caution by driving at reduced speed and keeping a safe distance.
questions.explanation: Drivers should anticipate doors opening or people emerging and pass a stopped vehicle cautiously with sufficient clearance and speed.

questions.question_en: When passing by a stopped school bus to let children getting off or on the bus, you checked to make sure they were safe but didn't slow down.

questions.question_en: Except when traveling on a priority road, you must not overtake a car or moped within 30 meters before a bicycle crossing.
questions.question_ja: 優先道路を通行しているとき以外は、自転車横断帯の手前30メートル以内の場所では、自動車や原動機付自転車を追越してはならない。
questions.explanation: False. The priority-road exception applies to the overtaking restriction near intersections, not to the 30-meter zone before a pedestrian or bicycle crossing. Overtaking there is prohibited.

questions.question_en: When shifting the selector to start an automatic car, it is enough to apply the parking brake; there is no need to press the brake pedal.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車を発進させるためにチェンジレバーを操作するときは、ハンドブレーキを引いていれば十分で、ブレーキペダルまで踏む必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. The brake pedal should be held firmly when selecting a driving range so the automatic car does not move unexpectedly.

questions.question_en: For an automatic car, the correct operation is to select “R” to move forward and “D” to reverse.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車は、前進のときはチェンジレバーを「R」に、後退するときは「D」に入れるのが正しい操作方法である。
questions.explanation: False. “D” is used for forward driving and “R” for reversing.

questions.question_en: Regulatory road markings are lines, symbols, or letters shown on the road surface with paint, road studs, and similar materials, and they prohibit or designate particular traffic movements.
questions.question_ja: 規制標示とは、ペイントや道路びょうなどによって路面に示された線、記号や文字のことをいい、特定の交通方法を禁止または指定するものである。
questions.explanation: True. Regulatory markings on the road surface are used to prohibit or specify particular methods of traffic.

questions.question_en: At a poorly visible intersection where a sign or marking requires a stop, if stopping at the stop line makes cross traffic hard to see, it is better to cross the stop line first and stop where you can check both directions.
questions.question_ja: 標識や標示によって一時停止となっている見通しの悪い交差点では、その手前の停止線で止まると、交差道路の車の接近がよく見えないので、はじめから停止線をこえて左右方向の安全が確認できる位置で止まった方がよい。
questions.explanation: False. You must first stop immediately before the stop line. If visibility is poor, you may then move forward carefully to a position where you can check safety.

questions.question_en: When approaching a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing, if it is clear that no pedestrian or bicycle is crossing, you may proceed without slowing or stopping.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道や自転車横断帯に近づいたとき、横断する人や自転車がいないことが明らかな場合は、徐行や一時停止せずに通行してもよい。
questions.explanation: True. The special requirement to approach at a speed that allows stopping applies when it is not clear that nobody will cross; if it is clearly empty, that requirement does not apply.

questions.question_en: When carrying a 12-year-old child in a car, the child must use a child seat.
questions.question_ja: 12歳のこどもを自動車に同乗させるときは、そのこどもにチャイルドシートを使用させなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The legal child-seat requirement applies to children under six years old, not to every 12-year-old.

questions.question_en: When changing lanes, you must check safety with mirrors and similar means, and it is also important to anticipate vehicles that may be in areas the mirrors cannot show.
questions.question_ja: 進路変更などをするときは、バックミラーなどで安全を確認しなければならないが、バックミラーなどで見えない部分にほかの車がいることを予測して運転することも大切である。
questions.explanation: True. Mirrors have blind spots, so a driver must also account for vehicles that may be hidden from mirror view.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that the number of lanes decreases ahead.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先で車線数が減少していることを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured warning sign indicates a reduction in the number of traffic lanes ahead.

questions.question_en: You must not use roller skates or skateboards in places with heavy traffic.
questions.question_ja: 交通量の多いところで、ローラースケートやスケートボードをしてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. Activities such as roller skating or skateboarding must not be done where they can obstruct or endanger traffic.

questions.question_en: Automatic cars do not require clutch operation and are therefore easier to drive than manual cars, so there is no need to take breaks even during long periods of driving.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車は、マニュアル車に比べてクラッチ操作がなく、その分操作の負担が軽く運転が楽になるので、長時間運転しても休息をとる必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. Driver fatigue and drowsiness still occur in an automatic car, so adequate rest is necessary during long drives.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates the beginning of a no-parking-and-no-stopping section, so from this sign onward you must not park or stop, except when stopping for a red signal or to avoid danger.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、駐停車禁止区間の「始まり」を表しているので、この標識がある場所からは、赤信号や危険防止のために一時停止する場合のほかは、駐停車してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. The supplementary indication marks the start of the restriction; necessary stops caused by traffic control or danger avoidance are not treated as prohibited parking or stopping.

questions.question_en: Overtaking requires complicated actions such as changing course and accelerating, but if you are experienced with the car and confident in your driving, some risky overtaking is permitted.
questions.question_ja: 追越しは、進路を変え、加速するなど複雑な運転操作を必要とするが、車に慣れ、運転に自信があれば多少無理な追越しをすることも許される。
questions.explanation: False. Confidence or experience does not justify an unsafe or forced overtake.

questions.question_en: In an automatic car, pressing the accelerator down sharply while driving automatically shifts to a lower gear and allows rapid acceleration.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車は、走行中にアクセルペダルを一気に踏み込むと、自動的に一段下のギアに変速され、急加速ができるようになっている。
questions.explanation: True. This is the automatic-transmission kick-down function, which selects a lower gear for stronger acceleration.

questions.question_en: This arrow signal is for streetcars, and vehicles other than streetcars cannot proceed on it.
questions.question_ja: この矢印の信号は、路面電車に対するものであって、路面電車以外は進むことはできない。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured arrow signal applies to streetcars; ordinary vehicles may not proceed merely because that streetcar signal is displayed.

questions.question_en: If you become sleepy after continuing monotonous driving for a long time, it is good to keep driving while looking at the scenery around the road.
questions.question_ja: 長時間単調な運転を続けて眠くなったときは、道路の周囲の景色を眺めながら運転を継続するのがよい。
questions.explanation: False. Drowsy driving is dangerous. You should stop in a safe place and rest rather than continue driving.

questions.question_en: When starting, first check safety, then signal with the turn indicator or similar device, and check the front, rear, left, and right again with mirrors and other means before moving off.
questions.question_ja: 発進するときは、発進する前に安全を確認してから方向指示器などで合図をし、もう一度バックミラーなどで前後左右の安全を確かめてから発進する。
questions.explanation: True. A safe start requires checking the surroundings, signalling, and making a final safety check before the vehicle moves.

questions.question_en: Stopping distance becomes longer as vehicle speed increases.
questions.question_ja: 停止距離は、車の速度が速くなれば速くなるほど、長くなる。
questions.explanation: True. Higher speed increases both the distance travelled before braking takes effect and the braking distance.

questions.question_en: On a winding mountain road with poor visibility, traffic was light and there was no oncoming vehicle, so I drove over into the right side of the road.
questions.question_ja: 曲がりくねった山道で見通しが悪かったが、交通量も少なく対向車もいなかったので、右側にはみ出して走行した。
questions.explanation: False. Poor visibility and light traffic do not permit unnecessary driving on the right side of the road.

questions.question_en: You must not drive after drinking alcohol, but it is acceptable to drive after drinking beer with a low alcohol content.
questions.question_ja: 酒を飲んで運転してはならないが、アルコール分の少ないビールであれば、飲んで運転してもかまわない。
questions.explanation: False. Driving after drinking is not permitted merely because the drink has a low alcohol content.

questions.question_en: Intersections and the areas around them have many traffic accidents, so you should increase speed and try to pass through quickly.
questions.question_ja: 交差点とその付近は、最も交通事故の発生が多い場所であるから速度を上げて、速く通過するよう心がける。
questions.explanation: False. Intersections require careful observation and an appropriate safe speed, not deliberate acceleration.

questions.question_en: When crossing a sidewalk to enter or leave a place outside the road, you must stop if pedestrians are present, but if there are none you may cross slowly without stopping.
questions.question_ja: 道路外に出るため歩道を横切るときは、歩行者がいるときは一時停止し、いなければ徐行で通行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. A vehicle crossing a sidewalk or roadside strip to enter or leave roadside premises must stop immediately before crossing it, even when no pedestrian is visible.

questions.question_en: The time to signal for a left turn, except at a roundabout, is when you reach a point 30 meters before the place where you will turn left.
questions.question_ja: 車が左折するとき（環状交差点を除く）の合図を行う時期は、左折しようとする地点から30メートル手前の地点に達したときである。
questions.explanation: True. The required left-turn signal is given from about 30 meters before the turning point.

questions.question_en: When a pedestrian is crossing at or near an intersection that has no pedestrian crossing, you must slow or stop as necessary so as not to obstruct the pedestrian.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道のない交差点やその付近を横断している歩行者があるときは、徐行したり一時停止して、その通行を妨げないようにしなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A driver must not interfere with a pedestrian crossing at or near such an intersection.

questions.question_en: You must not crowd sideways toward, or force your way in front of, a vehicle displaying the beginner-driver mark. (Excluding semi-medium vehicles.)
questions.question_ja: 「初心運転者標識」をつけて運転している者に対し、その車の側方に幅寄せをしたり、前方に無理に割り込んではならない。（準中型自動車を除く）
questions.explanation: True. Drivers must not unnecessarily cut in front of or crowd a protected beginner-mark vehicle.

questions.question_en: A route bus that had been stopped at a bus stop signalled that it was starting, so I slowed down and let the bus move out first.
questions.question_ja: 停留所で止まっていた路線バスが、方向指示器などで発進の合図をしたので、徐行してそのバスを先に発進させた。
questions.explanation: True. When a route bus signals to leave a stop, other drivers should not obstruct its departure unless avoiding it would create danger.

questions.question_en: When a police officer at an intersection gives a hand signal with both arms raised vertically, traffic parallel to the front of the officer’s body is facing the equivalent of a red light.
questions.question_ja: 警察官が交差点で手信号により両腕を垂直に上げているときは、警察官の身体の正面に平行する交通に対しては、赤色の灯火の信号と同じである。
questions.explanation: False. The meaning of a police officer’s hand signal depends on the direction of traffic relative to the officer. The stated direction and red-signal equivalence are not correct for this posture.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates a priority lane for route buses and similar vehicles, and other motor vehicles must not travel in a way that obstructs buses.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、路線バス等優先通行帯であることを表しており、ほかの自動車はバスの通行を妨げるような通行をしてはならない
questions.explanation: True. Other vehicles using a bus-priority lane must give priority to route buses and must not impede them.

questions.question_en: On a road with this sign, vehicles with a gross weight exceeding 5,500 kilograms cannot pass.
questions.question_ja: この標識がある道路では、総重量が5,500キログラムを超える車は通行することができない。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured weight-limit sign prohibits vehicles whose gross weight exceeds the displayed limit.

questions.question_en: To prepare for a person suddenly coming out from behind a stopped vehicle, it is useful to look carefully at places such as above the vehicle and under it.
questions.question_ja: 止まっている車のかげからの人の飛び出しに備えるためには、車の屋根や床下など注意深く見るとよい。
questions.explanation: True. Visible clues above or below a stopped vehicle can help reveal a pedestrian who is otherwise hidden behind it.

questions.question_en: When a road has a center line, vehicles must travel on the part of the road to the left of the center line.
questions.question_ja: 車は、道路に中央線があるときは、中央線から左の部分を通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. As a basic rule in Japan, vehicles travel on the left side of the road divided by the center line.

questions.question_en: A driver must not change course unnecessarily, but when a change is unavoidable it is important to check safety with mirrors and by direct observation.
questions.question_ja: 車を運転するときは、みだりに進路を変えてはいけないが、やむを得ず進路を変えるときは、バックミラーや目視で安全を確かめることが大切である。
questions.explanation: True. A lane or course change should be made only after confirming that it can be done safely, including blind-spot checks.

questions.question_en: When a person carrying a white or yellow cane, or a person with a guide dog, is walking, you must stop or slow down so that the person can pass safely.
questions.question_ja: 白や黄のつえを持った人や盲導犬を連れた人が歩いているときは、それらの人が安全に通行できるように、一時停止または徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Drivers must take special care around visually impaired pedestrians and stop or slow as necessary to protect their passage.

questions.question_en: If you obey the traffic laws while driving, it cannot be helped even if you cause people living along the road trouble through noise or similar disturbance.
questions.question_ja: 交通法規を守って運転していれば、たとえ沿道の人達に騒音などの迷惑がかかるとしてもやむを得ない。
questions.explanation: False. Drivers must also avoid unnecessary noise and nuisance; simply obeying other traffic rules does not excuse causing avoidable disturbance.

questions.question_en: When passing a pedestrian, I left a safe distance, but because it was raining I splashed muddy water on the pedestrian. The driver is responsible.
questions.question_ja: 歩行者のそばを通るとき、歩行者との間に安全な間隔をとったが、雨が降っていたため泥水を歩行者にはねた。この責任は、その車の運転者にある。
questions.explanation: True. A driver must take care not to splash pedestrians with mud or water and may be responsible for doing so.

questions.question_en: While driving, my mobile phone rang. There was nowhere to stop, so I had no choice but to hold the phone and talk while continuing to drive.
questions.question_ja: 自動車を運転中に携帯電話が鳴り、停車できる場所がなかったので、仕方なく運転しながら携帯電話を手に持って話をした。
questions.explanation: False. Holding and using a mobile phone while driving is prohibited; the driver should stop safely before using it.

questions.question_en: Overtaking is prohibited on curves and at road corners, but if the vehicle ahead is travelling below the prescribed speed, it is acceptable to overtake it.
questions.question_ja: カーブや曲がり角では、追越しが禁止されているが、前の車が定められた速度より遅い速度で走行しているときは、追越してもかまわない。
questions.explanation: False. A slow vehicle ahead does not cancel an overtaking prohibition at a location where overtaking is prohibited.

questions.question_en: This sign is the elderly-driver mark.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、高齢者マークである。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured mark is the mark used for elderly drivers.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates a pedestrian crossing.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、横断歩道であることを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured sign indicates a pedestrian crossing.

questions.question_en: When driving immediately behind a large vehicle, the road ahead cannot be seen, so for safety it is better to travel partly outside your traffic lane.
questions.question_ja: 大型車などの直後を走行するときは、前方の状況が見えないので、安全のため車両通行帯からはみ出して通行するのがよい。
questions.explanation: False. You must stay within the proper lane and instead keep enough following distance to improve visibility and safety.

questions.question_en: If traffic ahead is congested and you would have to stop on a pedestrian crossing, bicycle crossing, or railway crossing, you must stop before it.
questions.question_ja: 前方の交通が混雑して、横断歩道、自転車横断帯、踏切で停止することとなる場合は、その手前で停止しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. You must not enter such a crossing when congestion would leave your vehicle stopped on it.

questions.question_en: When driving, you should routinely prepare for emergencies by obtaining automobile insurance, learning first-aid procedures, and keeping emergency supplies in the vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 車を運転するときは、万一の場合に備えて自動車保険に加入したり、応急救護処置に必要な知識を身につけたり、救急用具を車に備えるように平素から心がけるようにする。
questions.explanation: True. These preparations help reduce harm and allow an appropriate response if an accident or emergency occurs.

questions.question_en: When crossing a railway crossing, you must stop immediately before it, or before the stop line if there is one, and check safety to both sides with your own eyes and ears, for example by opening a window or lowering the car-stereo volume.
questions.question_ja: 踏切を通過するときは、踏切の直前（停止線があるときは、その直前）で一時停止をし、車の窓を開けたり、カーステレオのボリュームを下げるなどして、自分の目と耳で左右の安全を確かめなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The basic rule is to stop before the crossing and directly confirm that it is safe before entering.

questions.question_en: Areas near road bends, near the crest of an uphill slope, and on steep downhill slopes are places where vehicles must proceed slowly.
questions.question_ja: 道路の曲がり角付近や上り坂の頂上付近やこう配の急な下り坂は、徐行場所である。
questions.explanation: True. These are designated locations where a vehicle must slow down because visibility or vehicle control may be limited.

questions.question_en: You must obey the signal facing you; you must not start merely because the signal to the side has turned red.
questions.question_ja: 信号は対面する信号に従うのであって、横の信号が赤になったからといって発進してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A driver follows the signal controlling that driver’s direction, not a signal intended for cross traffic.

questions.question_en: If you hold an ordinary driver’s license, you may drive a cargo vehicle with a maximum load of 3,000 kilograms and a passenger vehicle with seating for 11 people.
questions.question_ja: 普通免許を受けていれば、最大積載量が3,000キログラムの貨物自動車、乗車定員11人の乗用自動車を運転することができる。
questions.explanation: False. An ordinary license does not cover a vehicle with an 11-person capacity, and its vehicle/load limits are lower than the figures stated.

questions.question_en: When turning right at an intersection, except a roundabout, a motorcycle may travel straight from behind an oncoming vehicle and be hidden from view, so you must proceed with sufficient care.
questions.question_ja: 交差点（環状交差点を除く）で右折しようとするときは、対向車のかげから二輪車が直進してくる場合があり、危険であるから十分に注意して通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. An oncoming vehicle can conceal a motorcycle or other road user, so a right-turning driver must check carefully before crossing the oncoming path.

questions.question_en: An automatic car needs no clutch operation and can be steered with one hand, so it is acceptable to shave or apply makeup while driving.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車は、クラッチ操作がいらずハンドルも片手で操作できるので、運転中にひげをそったり化粧をしたりしてもかまわない。
questions.explanation: False. A driver must concentrate on safe vehicle control and may not engage in distracting activity that interferes with driving.

questions.question_en: When overtaking, it is best to close the following distance to the vehicle ahead as much as possible, then accelerate hard and change course from immediately behind it.
questions.question_ja: 追越しをする場合は、前の車との車間距離をできるだけ詰めておいて、その直近から一気に加速して進路変更するのがよい。
questions.explanation: False. You should keep a safe following distance, check ahead and behind, and make a smooth, safe overtaking manoeuvre rather than closing dangerously on the vehicle ahead.

questions.question_en: When driving, wearing geta sandals or high heels can interfere with sudden vehicle operation in an emergency and prevent safe driving.
questions.question_ja: 車を運転するとき、げたやハイヒールをはいて運転すると、緊急のとき、とっさの運転操作の支障となり安全運転ができない。
questions.explanation: True. Footwear that prevents reliable pedal operation can interfere with safe and immediate control of the vehicle.

questions.question_en: When passing beside a stopped vehicle, there is no need to pay attention to whether anyone is inside that vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 止まっている車のそばを通るとき、その車に人が乗っていないかなどまで注意する必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. A person in a stopped vehicle may open a door or step out, so a driver must watch the vehicle and its occupants when passing.

questions.question_en: When another vehicle is overtaking you and it does not have enough room to complete the overtake, you must move as far left as possible and give way.
questions.question_ja: ほかの車に追越されるとき、相手に追越しをするための十分な余地がない場合は、できるだけ左に寄り、進路をゆずらなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The vehicle being overtaken must not obstruct the overtake and, when necessary, should keep left to provide sufficient room.

questions.question_en: When opening a vehicle door, first open it slightly and pause, check behind, and then get out.
questions.question_ja: 車のドアを開けるときは、ドアを少し開けて一度止め、後方を確認してから降りるようにする。
questions.explanation: True. Opening the door in stages and checking behind helps prevent a collision with approaching vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians.

questions.question_en: When approaching a pedestrian crossing, it was not clear whether anyone was going to cross, but I passed at the same speed.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道に近づいたとき、横断する人がいるかどうか明らかではなかったが、そのままの速度で通過した。
questions.explanation: False. If it is not clear that nobody will cross, you must approach at a speed that allows you to stop before the crossing.

questions.question_en: While driving, I became lost, so I kept driving while staring at the car’s navigation screen.
questions.question_ja: 車を運転中、道に迷ったので、車に備え付けのカーナビゲーションを注視しながら運転した。
questions.explanation: False. A driver must not stare at a navigation display while the vehicle is moving because it takes attention away from the road.

questions.question_en: When passing a pedestrian or bicycle, if you leave a safe distance between you and them, you do not have to slow down.
questions.question_ja: 歩行者や自転車のそばを通るときは、歩行者などとの間に安全な間隔をあければ徐行しなくてもよい。
questions.explanation: True. The rule requires either a safe lateral distance or sufficiently slow speed; if a safe distance is maintained, slowing is not always required.

questions.question_en: On a road with traffic lanes, repeatedly changing lanes without reason can inconvenience following vehicles and can also cause an accident.
questions.question_ja: 車両通行帯のある道路では、みだりに通行帯を変えながら通行すると、後続車の迷惑となったり事故の原因にもなる。
questions.explanation: True. Unnecessary lane changes disrupt surrounding traffic and increase collision risk.

questions.question_en: When there are two traffic lanes in the same direction, an ordinary passenger car must travel in the right-hand lane.
questions.question_ja: 同一方向に二つの車両通行帯があるとき、普通自動車は、右側の車両通行帯を通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. As a basic rule, vehicles use the left lane and use the right lane mainly for overtaking or when traffic rules or road conditions require it.

questions.question_en: An incorrect or unnecessary signal can confuse other road users and create a dangerous situation, so care is required.
questions.question_ja: 誤った合図や不必要な合図は、ほかの道路利用者に迷いを与えるとともに、危険な状況におちいることがあるので注意する。
questions.explanation: True. Signals should be used correctly and only when needed so other road users can understand your intended movement.

questions.question_en: This road marking means that vehicles may pass through the marked area but must not stop within it.
questions.question_ja: この標示は、通行することはできるが、この中で停止してはならないことを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured marking is not merely a no-stopping area; vehicles are prohibited from entering the marked portion.

questions.question_en: For an automatic car, the correct selector positions are “D” for forward travel, “R” for reverse, and “P” for parking.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車のチェンジレバーの操作は、前進は「D」、後退は「R」、駐車は「P」に入れるのが正しい操作である。
questions.explanation: True. Those are the normal selector positions for forward driving, reversing, and parking.

questions.question_en: This marking indicates the center of the road or a center line.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、道路の中央であること、または中央線であることを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured road marking identifies the road center or center line.

questions.question_en: When starting an automatic car, it is dangerous to operate the selector without first confirming that the parking brake is applied and the selector is in P, and then firmly pressing the brake pedal.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車を発進させるときは、ハンドブレーキが引いてあり、チェンジレバーがPの位置にあることを確認してから、ブレーキペダルをしっかり踏んで操作しないと危険である。
questions.explanation: True. Confirming the parked condition and holding the brake helps prevent unintended movement when the driving range is selected.

questions.question_en: This sign means that because the road ahead is under construction, vehicles cannot pass.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先の道路が工事中のため、車は通行できないことを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured sign warns that road works are ahead; it does not by itself mean the road is closed to vehicles.

questions.question_en: Even near the crest of an uphill slope or on a steep downhill slope, it is acceptable to overtake if the vehicle being overtaken is a moped.
questions.question_ja: 車は、上り坂の頂上付近やこう配の急な下り坂でも、原動機付自転車であれば追越してよい。
questions.explanation: False. The overtaking restriction at such dangerous locations is not removed merely because the vehicle ahead is a moped.

questions.question_en: The driver must wear a seat belt, but passengers do not need to wear one.
questions.question_ja: シートベルトは、運転者自身が着用しなければならないが、同乗者は着用する必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. Seat-belt requirements apply to occupants as well as the driver, subject only to specific legal exceptions.

questions.question_en: At an intersection, if the signal facing you is flashing red, you may proceed slowly.
questions.question_ja: 交差点において、進行方向の信号が赤の点滅である場合は、徐行して通行する。
questions.explanation: False. A flashing red signal requires a vehicle to stop first and then proceed only after checking that it is safe.

questions.question_en: A provisional driving license is a license for a person seeking a first-class or second-class license who needs to drive a large, medium, semi-medium, or ordinary motor vehicle for practice or similar purposes.
questions.question_ja: 仮運転免許は、第一種運転免許または第二種運転免許を受けようとする者が、練習などのために大型自動車、中型自動車、準中型自動車または普通自動車を運転しようとする場合の免許をいう。
questions.explanation: True. A provisional license permits the specified practice driving before the full license is obtained, under the required conditions.

questions.question_en: Even if a driver is tired, the stopping distance does not become longer.
questions.question_ja: 運転者が疲れていても、停止距離が長くなるようなことはない。
questions.explanation: False. Fatigue can delay recognition and reaction, increasing the distance travelled before braking and therefore the total stopping distance.

questions.question_en: I was about to enter an intersection on a green signal, but a traffic officer controlling traffic instructed me to stop, so I entered the intersection and stopped inside it.
questions.question_ja: 青色の灯火の信号に従い交差点に入ろうとしたとき交通整理中の交通巡視員が「止まれ」の指示をしたので、交差点の中に入って停止した。
questions.explanation: False. An officer’s lawful traffic direction takes priority over the traffic signal, and the driver should stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question_en: An intersection where a sign requires a stop is a dangerous place where accidents can easily occur, so you must stop and check safety before proceeding.
questions.question_ja: 標識などで一時停止となっている交差点は、交通事故が起きやすい危険な場所であるので、必ず一時停止して安全を確認してから通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The stop requirement exists so the driver can confirm cross traffic and other hazards before entering.

questions.question_en: Even if an ordinary license is restricted to “ordinary vehicles with automatic transmission only,” after three years of driving experience the holder may drive every type of ordinary vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 普通免許で「普通車はAT車に限る」の免許条件がついていても、運転経歴が3年以上となったときには、すべての普通車の運転をすることができる。
questions.explanation: False. An AT-only license condition does not disappear with experience; the restriction must be formally removed before driving a manual vehicle.

questions.question_en: When overtaking requires part of your vehicle to enter the right side of the road center, you must keep the amount of encroachment as small as possible.
questions.question_ja: 追越しをするときに、車体が道路の中央から右側部分にはみ出す場合は、はみ出し方ができるだけ少なくなるようにしなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Any permitted use of the right side for overtaking should be limited to the minimum necessary and done safely.

questions.question_en: Where this sign is present, a vehicle must travel at a speed from which it can stop immediately.
questions.question_ja: この標識があるところでは、車はただちに停止できる速度で進行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured sign requires slow travel, meaning a speed that allows the vehicle to stop immediately.

questions.question_en: This road marking indicates that there is a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing ahead.
questions.question_ja: この標示は、前方に横断歩道または自転車横断帯があることを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured advance marking warns the driver of a pedestrian or bicycle crossing ahead.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that motor vehicles are prohibited from making a U-turn.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、自動車は転回できないことを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured regulatory sign prohibits turning around.

questions.question_en: When crossing a sidewalk or roadside strip to enter or leave property facing the road, the driver must stop immediately before crossing and must not obstruct pedestrians.
questions.question_ja: 道路に面した場所に出入りするために歩道や路側帯を横切る場合には、運転者はその直前で一時停止するとともに、歩行者の通行を妨げないようにしなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A vehicle entering or leaving roadside premises must stop before crossing the pedestrian area and give pedestrians priority.

questions.question_en: If you have a hangover and are dizzy, you must not drive a car even for a short distance.
questions.question_ja: 二日酔いで、めまいがしている状態の場合、近距離であっても車を運転してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A driver must not drive when physical condition or residual alcohol makes safe driving impossible.

questions.question_en: Overtaking is prohibited within 30 meters before and after a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道や自転車横断帯の前後30メートル以内は、追越しが禁止されている。
questions.explanation: False. The restriction applies to the crossing itself and the 30 meters before it; the statement incorrectly adds a 30-meter zone after the crossing.

questions.question_en: Where the traffic lane before an intersection is divided by a yellow line as shown, you must not cross the yellow line to change course, even to turn right or left.
questions.question_ja: この図のように、交差点の手前の車両通行帯が黄の線で区画されているところでは、たとえ右折や左折のためであっても、黄の線をこえて進路を変更してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A yellow lane-boundary line prohibits crossing it to change lanes, including a last-moment lane change for a turn.

questions.question_en: When the vehicle ahead is stopped or moving slowly at an intersection, railway crossing, or similar place, you must not cut in or cross in front of it.
questions.question_ja: 前方の車が交差点や踏切などで停止や徐行しているときは、その前に割り込んだり、横切ったりしてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. Cutting in ahead of vehicles waiting at such a location is prohibited and can create serious conflict with hidden traffic.

questions.question_en: A pedestrian was crossing near an intersection with no pedestrian crossing, so because it was dangerous I sounded the horn to make the pedestrian stop crossing.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道のない交差点のすぐ近くを、歩行者が横断していたが、危ないので警音器を鳴らして横断をやめさせた。
questions.explanation: False. The driver must avoid obstructing the pedestrian and adjust speed or stop as necessary; the horn is not to be used simply to force the pedestrian to give way.

questions.question_en: In addition to compulsory automobile liability insurance, it is better to have voluntary automobile insurance and to keep simple first-aid supplies in the vehicle in case of an emergency.
questions.question_ja: 自動車には、万一の場合に備えて自動車損害賠償責任保険（強制保険）のほかに任意保険をかけ、簡単な救急用具を備え付けておいた方がよい。
questions.explanation: True. Additional insurance and emergency supplies provide broader protection and help a driver respond appropriately after an accident.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates the end of a no-parking section.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、駐車禁止区間の「終わり」を表している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured supplementary indication marks the end of the parking prohibition.

questions.question_en: You must not install neon lights resembling traffic-signal colors near a signal, or publicity signs near road signs, in a way that makes traffic signals or signs difficult to recognize.
questions.question_ja: 信号機の近くに信号と似た色のネオンを設けたり、標識の近くに広報看板を設けるなどして、信号機や標識が認めにくいようにしてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. Objects that interfere with the visibility or recognition of official traffic-control devices can create danger and must not be placed that way.

questions.question_en: Many intersection accidents occur because drivers ignore rules such as signals or stop requirements, or fail to pay attention to other traffic.
questions.question_ja: 交差点での事故は、信号無視や一時不停止などルールを守らなかったり、ほかの交通に注意しないために起こすことが多い。
questions.explanation: True. Rule violations and inadequate observation are major causes of conflicts at intersections.

questions.question_en: When starting an automatic car, it is good to gradually release the brake pedal and, after the vehicle begins to move, press the accelerator gently.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車で発進するときのアクセルペダルの操作は、ブレーキペダルを徐々に放し、車が動き出してから、静かに踏むようにするのがよい。
questions.explanation: True. This smooth sequence uses the car’s creep movement and reduces the risk of sudden acceleration.

questions.question_en: If the left side of the road is at least 6 meters wide, it is acceptable to cross into the right side to overtake.
questions.question_ja: 道路の左側部分の幅が6メートル以上あれば、右側部分にはみ出して追越してもさしつかえない。
questions.explanation: False. The special permission to use the right side for overtaking is associated with a road whose left portion is less than 6 meters wide and only when the other legal conditions are met.

questions.question_en: When passing near an intersection or pedestrian crossing, pedestrians may cross at any time, so you must always sound the horn.
questions.question_ja: 交差点付近や横断歩道を通る場合は、いつ歩行者が横断するかわからないので、必ず警音器を鳴らす必要がある。
questions.explanation: False. The horn may be used only when required by a horn sign or when necessary to avoid danger, not routinely at every intersection or crossing.

questions.question_en: When an elderly driver displaying the elderly-driver mark or a disabled driver displaying the disabled-driver mark is driving, other vehicles are prohibited from overtaking or passing that vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 高齢者マークをつけている高齢運転者、身体障がい者マークをつけている身体の不自由な運転者が自動車を運転しているときは、追越しや追抜きが禁止されている。
questions.explanation: False. Overtaking itself is not categorically prohibited; what is prohibited is dangerous crowding or cutting in that interferes with protected marked vehicles.

questions.question_en: Vehicles must not travel on a road with this sign.
questions.question_ja: 車は、この標識のある道路を通行してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured sign prohibits the indicated vehicular traffic from using the road.

questions.question_en: A child seat should be selected to fit the child’s body size and to be capable of being securely fixed to the vehicle seat.
questions.question_ja: チャイルドシートは、こどもの体格に合い、座席に確実に固定できるものを選ぶとよい。
questions.explanation: True. Correct size and secure installation are essential for the restraint to protect the child properly.

questions.question_en: When passing near a person walking with a guide dog, you must stop or proceed slowly.
questions.question_ja: 盲導犬を連れた人が歩いているそばを通るときは、一時停止か徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Drivers must protect visually impaired pedestrians and stop or slow as necessary so they can travel safely.

questions.question_en: When turning right or left at an intersection, except a roundabout, the signal should be given from the point 30 meters before the place where the turn will be made.
questions.question_ja: 交差点（環状交差点を除く）で右折または左折をする場合の合図を行う場所は、その行為をしようとする地点から30メートル手前の地点に達したときである。
questions.explanation: True. The standard timing for a right- or left-turn signal is about 30 meters before the turning point.

questions.question_en: On a road with a lane reserved exclusively for route buses and similar vehicles, an ordinary motorcycle may always use the lane whenever bus traffic is light.
questions.question_ja: 路線バスなどの専用通行帯に指定されている道路で、路線バスなどの交通が少ないときは、普通自動二輪車はいつでも通行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. A bus-exclusive lane does not become freely available to an ordinary motorcycle merely because few buses are present; only vehicles permitted by the applicable rule may use it.

questions.question_en: At a place with this sign, you must not change course or pass alongside the vehicle ahead for the purpose of overtaking a motor vehicle or moped.
questions.question_ja: この標識がある場所では、自動車や原動機付自転車を追越すため、進路を変えたり、前の車の横を通り過ぎてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured sign prohibits overtaking in the regulated section.

questions.question_en: At a railway crossing, to avoid stalling, it is good to keep the same low gear used when starting and pass through without changing gear.
questions.question_ja: 踏切内では、エンストを防止するため、発進したときの低速ギアのまま一気に通過するのがよい。
questions.explanation: True. Maintaining a suitable low gear and avoiding gear changes on the crossing reduces the risk of stalling or stopping on the tracks.

questions.question_en: A vehicle’s difference between the paths of the front and rear wheels when turning disappears if the vehicle turns slowly.
questions.question_ja: 車の内輪差は、曲がるときに徐行すれば生じない。
questions.explanation: False. Off-tracking is caused by vehicle geometry and occurs even at low speed; slowing reduces danger but does not eliminate it.

questions.question_en: The distance a vehicle travels from the moment the driver senses danger and presses the brake until the brake actually begins to work is called the reaction distance.
questions.question_ja: 運転者が危険を感じてからブレーキを踏み、ブレーキが実際にきき始めるまでの間に走る距離を空走距離という。
questions.explanation: True. This is the distance travelled during the driver’s perception/reaction and the initial brake-response interval before effective braking begins.

questions.question_en: A person who has held an ordinary license for less than one year needs to display the beginner-driver mark at the specified front and rear positions only when driving on an expressway.
questions.question_ja: 普通免許を受けてから1年を経過していない者は、高速道路を通行する場合に限り、その車の前と後ろの定められた位置に「初心者マーク」をつければよい。
questions.explanation: False. The beginner mark is generally required when an eligible novice drives an ordinary vehicle during the first year, not only on expressways.

questions.question_en: You must not do things on the road that obstruct traffic, such as staggering around while drunk or standing and talking.
questions.question_ja: 道路上で酒に酔ってふらついたり、立ち話をしたりなどして交通の妨げとなるようなことはしてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. Road users must not create avoidable obstructions or danger on the roadway through conduct such as drunken wandering or standing in the traffic area.

questions.question_en: A large bus was travelling slowly on a winding mountain road. Although I was at a curve with poor visibility, I was in a hurry, so I crossed into the right side of the road and overtook it.
questions.question_ja: 曲がりくねった山道を大型バスがゆっくり走っており、見通しの悪いカーブであったが、急いでいたので右側部分にはみ出して追越した。
questions.explanation: False. Overtaking at a poorly visible curve is prohibited and dangerous; being in a hurry does not justify crossing to the right to pass.

questions.question_en: A provisional-license practice sign must be attached to either one of the designated positions at the front or rear of the vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 仮免許練習標識は、前後の定められた場所のいずれかにつけなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The required practice signs must be displayed at the designated positions on both the front and the rear.

questions.question_en: For an ordinary passenger car travelling at 60 km/h, the stopping distance on dry asphalt is about 20 meters.
questions.question_ja: 時速60キロメートルで走行している普通乗用自動車の停止距離は、乾燥したアスファルト道路の場合で、約20メートルとなる。
questions.explanation: False. At 60 km/h the total stopping distance is considerably more than 20 meters because it includes both reaction distance and braking distance.

questions.question_en: Vehicles and streetcars facing this signal may stop at the stopping position, check that it is safe, and then proceed.
questions.question_ja: この信号に対面する車や路面電車は、停止位置で一時停止し、安全確認をして進むことができる。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured flashing-red signal requires a vehicle or streetcar to stop first and permits proceeding only after confirming safety.

questions.question_en: When travelling more slowly than other vehicles, you should keep as far left as practicable and try not to disturb the flow of traffic.
questions.question_ja: ほかの車より遅い速度で走行する場合は、できるだけ道路の左寄りを走行し、交通の流れを乱さないように心がけるべきである。
questions.explanation: True. A slower vehicle should keep to the left so faster traffic can flow safely, unless another rule or road condition requires otherwise.

questions.question_en: If a passenger opens a door without checking safety and injures a cyclist or another road user passing beside the vehicle, the driver has absolutely no responsibility.
questions.question_ja: 乗車していたほかの者が安全を確認しないでドアを開け、側方を通過する自転車などの通行人にケガをさせた場合は、車の運転者に責任は全くない。
questions.explanation: False. The driver is responsible for safe vehicle use and should ensure that doors are not opened in a way that endangers passing traffic.

questions.question_en: When stopping before a pedestrian crossing, if there is a stop line you should stop immediately before that stop line.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道の手前で停止するときは、停止線があるときは停止線の直前で停止する。
questions.explanation: True. The stop line determines the required stopping position when one is provided.

questions.question_en: Where crossing the road or making a U-turn is prohibited by a sign or marking, reversing is automatically prohibited as well.
questions.question_ja: 標識や標示によって横断や転回が禁止されているところでは、同時に後退も禁止されている。
questions.explanation: False. A prohibition on crossing or making a U-turn does not by itself create a separate prohibition on reversing.

questions.question_en: While driving, it is safer to avoid unnecessary lane or course changes and travel smoothly with the overall flow of traffic.
questions.question_ja: 車を運転中は、不必要な進路変更はせずに、全体の車の流れに乗って走行した方が安全である。
questions.explanation: True. Stable, predictable travel reduces conflicts caused by unnecessary lateral movement.

questions.question_en: A seat belt does not have to be fastened when illness or another unavoidable circumstance makes its use impracticable.
questions.question_ja: シートベルトは、病気などやむを得ない場合は締めなくてもよい。
questions.explanation: True. Seat-belt rules contain limited exceptions for unavoidable circumstances such as certain medical conditions.

questions.question_en: Where there is no roadside strip or sidewalk, a vehicle must leave the road shoulder, 0.5 meter from the road edge, clear when travelling.
questions.question_ja: 路側帯や歩道がないところでは、路肩（路端から0.5メートル）をあけて通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The edge portion of the road is to be kept clear as required rather than being used as the normal travel path.

questions.question_en: This sign is the warning sign for “other danger.”
questions.question_ja: この標識は、「その他の危険」を示す警戒標識である。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured warning sign is used for a danger that is not represented by a more specific warning symbol.

questions.question_en: To use engine braking in an automatic car, it is good to move the selector to 2 or L, or to 1 where provided.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車でエンジンブレーキを用いるときは、チェンジレバーを２かＬ（または１）に入れるとよい。
questions.explanation: True. Selecting a lower range increases engine-braking effect, especially on a descent.

questions.question_en: When turning right at an intersection, if a sign or marking specifies the required method of travel, you must follow that instruction.
questions.question_ja: 交差点を右折する場合、標識などで通行方法が指定されているときは、それに従って通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Traffic signs and road markings that prescribe a particular movement take priority over the ordinary turning method.

questions.question_en: When turning left at an intersection in accordance with a signal, if there are no pedestrians crossing, you do not have to slow down.
questions.question_ja: 信号に従って交差点を左折するときは、横断する歩行者がいなければ徐行しなくてもよい。
questions.explanation: False. A left turn must be made at a sufficiently slow speed to turn safely, regardless of whether a pedestrian is currently visible.

questions.question_en: With a large special-vehicle license, you may drive large special vehicles, small special vehicles, and mopeds.
questions.question_ja: 大型特殊免許では、大型特殊自動車と小型特殊自動車と原動機付自転車を運転することができる。
questions.explanation: True. Those vehicle classes are included within the driving privileges of the large special-vehicle license.

questions.question_en: If an automatic car is likely to remain stopped for a long time, it is better to select “N” and apply the parking brake.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車を運転中、停止時間が長くなりそうなときは、チェンジレバーを「N」に入れ、ハンドブレーキをかけておいた方がよい。
questions.explanation: True. For a prolonged stop, selecting neutral and securing the vehicle with the parking brake can prevent unintended movement and reduce the need to hold the foot brake continuously.

questions.question_en: When a driver seated in the driving position looks outside, parts of the view are hidden by the vehicle body and other structures; these unseen areas are called blind spots.
questions.question_ja: 運転者が、運転席に座った状態で車の外を見た場合、視界が車体などで妨げられて見えない部分ができるが、この見えない部分を死角という
questions.explanation: True. A blind spot is an area around the vehicle that the driver cannot see directly or through the normal field of view.

questions.question_en: Even at a place with this sign, if visibility is good and there is no vehicle on the intersecting road, you may proceed without stopping.
questions.question_ja: この標識のある場所でも、見通しがよくて交差道路を通行している車がなければ、一時停止することなく進行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured stop sign requires a complete stop whether or not cross traffic is visible.

questions.question_en: Traffic rules are established as common rules for using roads safely, so even if you are confident you will not cause an accident, you should obey the prescribed traffic rules.
questions.question_ja: 交通規則は、道路を安全に通行するための「共通の約束ごと」として決められているものであるから、たとえ交通事故を起こさない自信があっても、決められた交通規則に従うべきである。
questions.explanation: True. Personal confidence does not replace the common rules that allow all road users to predict one another’s actions.

questions.question_en: When the vehicle ahead has moved toward the center of the road in order to turn right, another vehicle should pass on its left side.
questions.question_ja: 車は、前の車が右折するため道路の中央に寄って通行しているときは、その左側を通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A vehicle positioned toward the center for a right turn is passed on the left, provided this can be done safely and lawfully.

questions.question_en: When passing beside a bicycle, it is enough simply to reduce speed.
questions.question_ja: 車は、自転車のそばを通過するときは、スピードを落とせばよい。
questions.explanation: False. The driver must protect the cyclist by maintaining a safe lateral distance or, when sufficient distance cannot be kept, by proceeding at an appropriately slow speed; merely reducing speed without considering clearance is not enough.

questions.question_en: When approaching a clearly visible pedestrian crossing where a pedestrian is already crossing, the driver may decide it is safe and pass through slowly.
questions.question_ja: 歩行者が横断している見通しがよい横断歩道に近づいたときは、運転者が安全であると判断すれば、徐行してその場を通過することができる。
questions.explanation: False. A pedestrian using the crossing has priority; the vehicle must stop and must not obstruct the pedestrian’s crossing.

questions.question_en: When riding a motorcycle straight through an intersection, except a roundabout, be careful because an oncoming four-wheeled vehicle turning right may have difficulty seeing you.
questions.question_ja: 二輪車で交差点（環状交差点を除く）を直進するときは、右折する対向の四輪車から見えにくいので注意して進行する。
questions.explanation: True. Motorcycles can be hidden by other vehicles or be misjudged by a right-turning driver, so defensive observation is important.

questions.question_en: At a place with this sign, an ordinary car is also prohibited from overtaking a moped.
questions.question_ja: この標識のあるところでは、普通自動車が原動機付自転車を追越すことも禁止されている。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured no-overtaking restriction applies to overtaking the covered vehicles, including a moped.

questions.question_en: When giving way to an emergency vehicle on a road away from an intersection, it is not always necessary to stop; moving to the left side of the road is sufficient when that safely gives it a clear path.
questions.question_ja: 近くに交差点のない道路で緊急自動車に進路をゆずるときは、必ずしも一時停止しなくても道路の左側に寄ればよい。
questions.explanation: True. Away from an intersection, the basic requirement is to move to the left and give way; a complete stop is not automatically required.

questions.question_en: There was a vehicle stopped just before a pedestrian crossing, but nobody was crossing, so I slowed down and passed it.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道の手前で止まっている車があったが、横断している人がいなかったので徐行して通過した。
questions.explanation: False. Before passing alongside a vehicle stopped immediately before a pedestrian crossing, you must first stop and check for a pedestrian who may be hidden by that vehicle.

questions.question_en: While this signal is displayed, a pedestrian may begin crossing if there are no vehicles passing.
questions.question_ja: この信号が表示されているとき、歩行者は通行車両がなければ横断を開始することができる。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured pedestrian signal does not permit a pedestrian to begin crossing; the absence of vehicles does not override the signal.

questions.question_en: Holding a driver’s license means not only that you can operate a vehicle; you must also recognize the social responsibilities involved, including criminal, administrative, and civil responsibility.
questions.question_ja: 運転免許を持つということは、単に車を運転できるということだけでなく、刑事上、行政上、民事上の責任など、社会的責任があることを自覚しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A licensed driver can bear multiple forms of legal and social responsibility for driving conduct and accidents.

questions.question_en: When practicing with a provisional license, it is good to practice on especially congested roads or school routes so that you improve quickly.
questions.question_ja: 仮免許で練習のため運転するときは、早く上達するために、特に交通の混雑している道路や通学路などで行うとよい。
questions.explanation: False. Practice driving should avoid unnecessarily dangerous environments such as heavily congested roads and school routes.

questions.question_en: This road marking represents a “no-entry area.”
questions.question_ja: この標示は、「立入り禁止部分」を表している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured marking has a different regulatory meaning; it is not the road marking designated as a no-entry area.

questions.question_en: Near the crest of a hill, visibility is poor and the location is dangerous, so you must proceed slowly.
questions.question_ja: 坂道の頂上付近は見通しが悪く危険なので、徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The area near the crest of a slope is a designated slow-speed location because the road ahead is difficult to see.

questions.question_en: The traffic light ahead changed to yellow, so I pressed the brake several times to alert the following vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 前方の信号が黄色になったので、ブレーキを数回に分けて踏み、後続車に注意をうながした。
questions.explanation: True. Repeated light braking can illuminate the brake lamps and warn following traffic that you are slowing, while avoiding an abrupt stop when conditions permit.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates a minimum speed of 50 km/h.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、最低速度が時速50キロメートルであることを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured circular 50 sign indicates a maximum speed of 50 km/h, not a minimum speed.
