questions.question_en: When the road surface is poor, the vehicle is carrying a heavy load, or the tires are worn, you should pay particular attention to speed and following distance.
questions.question_ja: 路面の状況が悪いとき、重い荷物を積んでいるときやタイヤがすり減っているときは、速度や車間距離に注意する。
questions.explanation: True. These conditions can reduce grip or increase the distance needed to stop, so lower speed and greater spacing may be necessary.

questions.question_en: On a road with this sign, large and ordinary motorcycles cannot pass, but mopeds may pass.
questions.question_ja: この標識のある道路では、大型自動二輪車や普通自動二輪車は通行できないが、原動機付自転車は通行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured prohibition covers two-wheeled motor vehicles and mopeds; a moped is not exempt.

questions.question_en: For a motor vehicle or moped changing its course to the left while travelling in the same direction, the signal should be given about three seconds before the course change.
questions.question_ja: 自動車や原動機付自転車が、同じ方向に進行しながら進路を左方に変えるときの合図の時期は、進路を変えようとするときの約3秒前である。
questions.explanation: True. A lane or course-change signal is given approximately three seconds before beginning the change.

questions.question_en: When parking an automatic car on an uphill slope, keep the brake pedal depressed, apply the parking brake securely, and then move the selector to P.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車を上り坂で駐車するときは、ブレーキペダルを踏んだままハンドブレーキを確実に引いてから、チェンジレバーをPに入れる。
questions.explanation: True. Securing the car with the brake and parking brake before selecting P helps prevent unintended movement and avoids relying only on the transmission parking mechanism.

questions.question_en: I was driving an ordinary passenger car in an open bus-priority lane. A bus approached from behind, but because it was not a bus-exclusive lane I continued driving in the lane.
questions.question_ja: 路線バス等優先通行帯があいていたので普通乗用車で通行していたところ、後方からバスが近づいてきたが、バスの専用通行帯でないので、そのまま進行した。
questions.explanation: False. A vehicle in a bus-priority lane must leave the lane promptly when a route bus approaches if remaining there would obstruct the bus.

questions.question_en: At an uncontrolled intersection where the roads are about the same width, except a roundabout, you must not obstruct a vehicle approaching from the left.
questions.question_ja: 交通整理の行われていない道路幅が同じような交差点（環状交差点を除く）では、左方からくる車の進行を妨げてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. At such an intersection, the vehicle approaching from the left has priority under the basic left-priority rule.

questions.question_en: The vehicle ahead signalled a right turn and was moving toward the right, so I sounded the horn to warn it and overtook it on its right side.
questions.question_ja: 前の車が右折の合図をし、右側に進路を変えようとしていたので、警音器を鳴らして注意をうながし、その車の右側を追越した。
questions.explanation: False. You must not pass on the right of a vehicle that is positioning or signalling to turn right; the horn also does not create a right to make that unsafe overtake.

questions.question_en: When an automatic car’s selector is in P or N, the vehicle may start moving because of creep.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車のチェンジレバーがPまたはNの位置にあるときは、クリープ現象によって車が動き出すことがある。
questions.explanation: False. Creep occurs when a driving range such as D or R is engaged; it does not normally propel the vehicle with the selector in P or N.

questions.question_en: If you carry a photocopy of your driver’s license, your identity can be confirmed, so you do not need to carry the original license while driving.
questions.question_ja: 運転免許証のコピーを持っていれば、運転者を確認できるので、運転中本物の運転免許証は持たなくてもよい。
questions.explanation: False. A driver who is required to hold a license must carry the valid license itself as required; a photocopy is not a substitute.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates a pedestrian crossing and a bicycle crossing.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、横断歩道と自転車横断帯であることを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured sign identifies a location with both a pedestrian crossing and a bicycle crossing.

questions.question_en: Inside a tunnel that has traffic lanes, overtaking is permitted.
questions.question_ja: 車両通行帯のあるトンネルの中では、追越しをすることができる。
questions.explanation: True. The general tunnel overtaking prohibition applies to a tunnel without traffic lanes; in a lane-marked tunnel, overtaking is not prohibited solely because it is a tunnel, although any other restriction still applies.

questions.question_en: A streetcar was stopped, but there were no passengers in the safety island, so I passed it without changing my manner of travel.
questions.question_ja: 路面電車が停止していたが、安全地帯に乗降客がいなかったので、そのまま通過した
questions.explanation: False. Even where a safety island permits passing a stopped streetcar, the vehicle must pass carefully at low speed rather than simply continuing normally.

questions.question_en: On a road marked as a school route, a child may suddenly run out from behind a parked vehicle, so it is important to drive with particular care.
questions.question_ja: 通学路の標識のある道路では、駐車車両のかげからこどもが急に飛び出してくることが予測されるので、特に注意して走行することが大切である。
questions.explanation: True. School routes require heightened anticipation of children whose movements may be sudden or hidden by parked vehicles.

questions.question_en: When a hearing-impaired driver displaying this mark is driving an ordinary or semi-medium vehicle, you must not crowd alongside or force your way in front of that vehicle except when unavoidable to prevent danger.
questions.question_ja: このマークをつけた聴覚障がいのある運転者が普通自動車や準中型自動車を運転しているときは、危険をさけるためやむを得ない場合のほか、その車の側方に幅寄せしたり、無理に割り込んではならない。
questions.explanation: True. Vehicles displaying the hearing-impaired-driver mark are protected from unnecessary crowding and cutting in.

questions.question_en: Unless a sign or marking specifies otherwise, the maximum speed for a moped is 30 km/h.
questions.question_ja: 原動機付自転車の最高速度は、標識などによる指定がなければ時速30キロメートルである。
questions.explanation: True. The statutory maximum speed for a general moped is 30 km/h unless a lower applicable restriction governs.

questions.question_en: The “Road Closed” sign prohibits pedestrians from passing for safety reasons, so motor vehicles may pass.
questions.question_ja: 「通行止め」の道路標識は、危険防止のため歩行者の通行を禁止するものであるから、自動車は通行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. A road-closed sign prohibits the traffic covered by that closure; it does not mean that motor vehicles are allowed through while only pedestrians are prohibited.

questions.question_en: On a road without traffic lanes, faster vehicles must generally travel nearer the center of the road.
questions.question_ja: 車両通行帯のない道路では原則として、速度の速い車は中央寄りの部分を通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. Vehicles should generally keep to the left; speed does not create a rule requiring faster vehicles to travel near the road center.

questions.question_en: When driving a motor vehicle, you must not exceed the maximum speed shown by traffic signs or road markings.
questions.question_ja: 自動車を運転する場合は、標識や標示で示されている最高速度をこえて運転してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A posted or marked maximum speed is the legal upper speed limit for vehicles to which it applies.

questions.question_en: If a vehicle is stopped at or immediately before a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing, you must stop before passing beside that vehicle and moving ahead of it.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道または自転車横断帯やその直前に止まっている車があるときは、そのそばを通って前方に出る前に一時停止をしなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The stopped vehicle may hide a pedestrian or cyclist, so a driver must first stop before passing it at the crossing.

questions.question_en: The lower the gear used for engine braking, the weaker the braking effect becomes.
questions.question_ja: エンジンブレーキは、低速ギアになるほど制動力は小さくなる。
questions.explanation: False. A lower gear generally produces stronger engine braking.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates the stopping position for vehicles, so it has the same meaning as a stop line shown by a white line on the road.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、車両の停止位置を示すものであるから、道路に白線で示されている停止線と同じである。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured sign designates the point before which a vehicle must stop, serving the same stopping-position function as a road stop line.

questions.question_en: This sign before an intersection indicates that the road I am travelling on is a priority road.
questions.question_ja: 交差点の手前のこの標識は、自分の通行している道路が「優先道路」であることを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured indication shows that the driver’s road has priority through the intersection.

questions.question_en: When travelling according to designated lane directions near an intersection, you do not need to give way even if an emergency vehicle approaches.
questions.question_ja: 交差点付近を指定通行区分によって通行しているときは、緊急自動車が接近してきても、進路をゆずる必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. The duty to give way to an approaching emergency vehicle takes precedence; a designated lane direction does not cancel that duty.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates the end of a maximum-speed restriction of 50 km/h.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、最高速度50キロメートル毎時の規制の終わりを表している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured sign marks the termination of the displayed 50 km/h maximum-speed regulation.

questions.question_en: I drove a truck with a maximum payload of 3 tons past this sign.
questions.question_ja: この標識のあるところで最大積載量3トンのトラックを運転して通行した。
questions.explanation: True. The truck’s maximum payload does not exceed the load limit displayed by the pictured sign, so the stated passage is permitted.

questions.question_en: A vehicle’s brakes work better if it is driven over its weight limit.
questions.question_ja: 重量制限をこえて走行した方が、ブレーキのききがよくなる。
questions.explanation: False. Excess weight increases the load the brakes must control and can lengthen stopping distance or reduce safe braking performance.

questions.question_en: When overtaking a moped, it is important to keep sufficient lateral distance so that air pressure from your vehicle does not cause the rider to fall.
questions.question_ja: 原動機付自転車を追越すときは、車の風圧などのために相手が転倒することのないように、十分な側方間隔を保って追越すことが大切である。
questions.explanation: True. Two-wheeled vehicles can be destabilized by close passing and vehicle air movement, so ample side clearance is necessary.

questions.question_en: I lost my driver’s license, but as long as I report it to the police I may continue driving until a replacement license is issued.
questions.question_ja: 運転免許証をなくしたが、警察官に届け出さえすれば、免許証の再交付を受けるまでの期間でも車を運転してよい。
questions.explanation: False. Reporting the loss does not substitute for the requirement to possess and carry a valid license while driving.

questions.question_en: When driving through a place with many pedestrians, you should keep sounding the horn.
questions.question_ja: 歩行者の多い場所を通行するときは、警音器を鳴らしながら通る。
questions.explanation: False. The horn is not for routine use around pedestrians; it is used only where required or when necessary to avoid danger.

questions.question_en: The traffic signal facing me was red, but a police officer gave a hand signal instructing me to proceed, so I followed the officer’s signal and went through.
questions.question_ja: 対面する信号機の信号が赤であったが、警察官が手信号で「進め」の合図をしたので、その手信号に従って進行した。
questions.explanation: True. A police officer’s traffic direction takes precedence over an ordinary traffic-light indication.

questions.question_en: You must not cut in front of, or cross in front of, a vehicle that is slowing down to avoid danger.
questions.question_ja: 危険防止のため徐行している車の前に割り込んだり、その前を横切ったりしてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. Interfering with a vehicle that is taking evasive safety action can create an immediate collision risk and is prohibited.

questions.question_en: In a roadside strip with this marking, vehicles may not park or stop, and light vehicles may not travel there either.
questions.question_ja: この標示のある路側帯では、車の駐停車はもちろん軽車両の通行もできない。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured roadside-strip marking designates a pedestrian-protected strip that vehicles, including light vehicles, must not use for travel and where motor-vehicle parking or stopping is not permitted.

questions.question_en: When passing near a person carrying a white or yellow cane, you must stop or proceed slowly.
questions.question_ja: 白や黄色のつえを持った人が歩いているそばを通るときは、一時停止か徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Such a cane identifies a person who may have a visual impairment, so drivers must take protective action to ensure safe passage.

questions.question_en: If the trip will only take a short time, the driver and passengers do not need to wear seat belts.
questions.question_ja: シートベルトは、運転して行く先が短時間であれば運転者または同乗者は着用しなくてもよい
questions.explanation: False. Trip duration does not create an exemption from the seat-belt requirement.

questions.question_en: When overtaking, if you have even some uncertainty about the vehicle ahead or the traffic situation, it is better not to hesitate and to overtake quickly in one move.
questions.question_ja: 追越しをするとき、前の車の動きや前方の交通などに多少の不安がある場合には、ためらうことなく一気に追越した方がよい。
questions.explanation: False. If there is uncertainty about safety, you should not begin the overtake; overtaking should be attempted only when the route and surrounding traffic are clearly safe.

questions.question_en: Overtaking near the crest of an uphill slope is prohibited because there is a risk of colliding with a vehicle coming from the opposite direction.
questions.question_ja: 上り坂の頂上付近での追越しは、反対方向の車などと衝突するおそれがあるので禁止されている。
questions.explanation: True. Visibility beyond the crest is restricted, making an overtake unsafe and therefore prohibited there.

questions.question_en: When a winter road is frozen, sudden braking can easily cause a skid, so it is safer to drive below the speed limit.
questions.question_ja: 冬道で路面が凍りついた状態になっていると、急停止したとき横すべりしやすいので、制限速度以下で運転する方が安全である。
questions.explanation: True. A posted limit is only an upper limit; on ice, the safe speed can be much lower and stopping inputs should be gentle.

questions.question_en: Immediately after starting the engine of an automatic car, engine speed may be high and releasing the accelerator alone may not slow the car sufficiently, so care is required.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車でのエンジン始動直後の走行は、エンジンの回転数が高く、アクセルペダルから足を放しただけでは十分に減速できないことがあるので注意する。
questions.explanation: True. Elevated engine speed after a cold start can increase creep or reduce the expected deceleration, so the driver should control the vehicle carefully with the brake.

questions.question_en: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection where your road crosses a wider road, there is no particular need to slow down.
questions.question_ja: 道幅が広い道路と交差する交通整理の行われていない交差点（環状交差点を除く）を進行する場合は、特に徐行する必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. At an uncontrolled intersection where the intersecting road is clearly wider, the driver must proceed cautiously and must not obstruct traffic on the wider road; slowing is required where the rules designate it.

questions.question_en: At a place with this sign, you may overtake as long as you do not cross into the right side of the road.
questions.question_ja: この標識のあるところでは、右側部分にはみ出さなければ追越してもよい。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured restriction prohibits crossing into the right side for the purpose of overtaking; it does not prohibit every overtake that can be completed without crossing the prohibited boundary.

questions.question_en: A driver must always slow down when passing a pedestrian crossing, even if there is no pedestrian there.
questions.question_ja: 車の運転者は、横断歩道に歩行者がいなくても徐行して通過しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. If it is clearly apparent that no pedestrian or bicycle will cross, the special approach-slowing requirement does not apply.

questions.question_en: When changing course on a moped, consider the movements of other vehicles, confirm safety, and signal about three seconds before changing course.
questions.question_ja: 原動機付自転車で進路変更するときは、ほかの自動車などの動きを十分に考え、安全を確認し、進路を変えようとするときの約3秒前に合図をする。
questions.explanation: True. Course-change signals are given approximately three seconds before beginning the movement, after checking that it can be made safely.

questions.question_en: On a rainy day, splashing mud or water onto a pedestrian cannot be avoided, so the driver is not responsible.
questions.question_ja: 雨の日に、泥や水を歩行者にはねても避けようがないので、運転者の責任ではない。
questions.explanation: False. A driver must adjust speed and position to avoid splashing pedestrians; rain does not remove that responsibility.

questions.question_en: Opening a vehicle door slightly at first when getting out also serves as a signal to other passing vehicles.
questions.question_ja: 車から降りるためにドアを最初少し開ける動作は、通行するほかの車への合図にもなる。
questions.explanation: True. A small initial opening can make the intention to open the door more visible, while allowing another safety check before the door is opened fully.

questions.question_en: If you hold a large-motorcycle license, you may drive a large motorcycle, ordinary motorcycle, small special vehicle, and moped.
questions.question_ja: 大型二輪の免許を受けていれば、大型自動二輪車、普通自動二輪車、小型特殊自動車、原動機付自転車を運転することができる。
questions.explanation: True. Those vehicle classes are included in the driving privileges associated with a large-motorcycle license.

questions.question_en: If you hold a large-special-vehicle license, you may tow another vehicle without a towing license regardless of the towed vehicle’s total weight.
questions.question_ja: 大型特殊免許を受けていれば、けん引免許がなくても、その車の総重量に関係なくけん引することができる。
questions.explanation: False. A separate towing license is generally required when the towed vehicle exceeds the applicable weight threshold, apart from specified exceptions.

questions.question_en: When a streetcar is stopped at a stop that has no safety island, you must remain stopped until passengers have finished getting on and off.
questions.question_ja: 安全地帯のない停留所で、路面電車が止まっているときは、人の乗り降りが終わるまで、一時停止していなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Without a safety island, passengers move between the streetcar and roadside, so vehicles must stop to protect them while they board or alight.

questions.question_en: The hand signal for reversing is made by extending the arm diagonally downward outside the vehicle, turning the palm toward the rear, and moving the arm back and forth.
questions.question_ja: 後退するときの手の合図は、腕を車の外に出して斜め下にのばし、手のひらを後ろに向け腕を前後に動かす。
questions.explanation: True. That is the prescribed hand signal indicating a reverse movement.

questions.question_en: At an intersection, if the signal facing your direction is flashing red, you must proceed slowly while checking that the intersection is safe.
questions.question_ja: 交差点において、進行方向の信号が赤色の灯火の点滅をしている場合は、交差点の安全を確認しながら徐行して通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. A flashing red signal requires a complete stop first; proceeding slowly without stopping is insufficient.

questions.question_en: When traffic is light, it is acceptable to hold and use a mobile phone while driving.
questions.question_ja: 交通量が少ないときは、走行しながら携帯電話を手に持って使用してもよい。
questions.explanation: False. Light traffic does not create an exception to the prohibition on holding and using a phone while driving.

questions.question_en: A vehicle must not overtake a motor vehicle or moped at a railway crossing or within 30 meters before it.
questions.question_ja: 車は、踏切とその手前から30メートル以内の場所で、自動車や原動機付自転車を追越してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. Railway crossings and the 30-meter approach area are locations where overtaking is prohibited.

questions.question_en: A person who has held an ordinary license for less than one year must display the beginner-driver mark at either the designated front position or the designated rear position of the vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 普通免許を受けて1年を経過していない者は、「初心者マーク」を、自動車の前か後ろどちらかの定められた位置につけて運転しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The beginner-driver mark must be displayed at the designated positions on both the front and the rear.

questions.question_en: Crossing the road, making a U-turn, or reversing can run against the normal traffic flow, so a driver must take sufficient care not to obstruct the normal movement of pedestrians or other vehicles.
questions.question_ja: 車が横断、転回、後退したりすることは、交通の流れに逆らう運転になるので、歩行者やほかの車の正常な交通を妨げないように十分注意する必要がある。
questions.explanation: True. These movements create unusual conflicts with normal traffic and must be made only when they can be completed without obstruction or danger.

questions.question_en: At a place with this sign, there is an intersection, so you must sound the horn as you proceed.
questions.question_ja: この標識のあるところでは、交差点があるので、警音器を鳴らして進行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured sign warns of an intersection; it does not by itself require horn use.

questions.question_en: When turning left at an intersection, it is better to steer right first and then turn left in order to eliminate the vehicle’s off-tracking.
questions.question_ja: 交差点を左折するときは、車の内輪差をなくすため、いったん右にハンドルを切ってから左折した方がよい。
questions.explanation: False. Swinging right before a left turn creates danger and does not eliminate off-tracking. The driver should move toward the left edge in advance and turn slowly while checking the left side.

questions.question_en: When driving a motor vehicle, a valid vehicle inspection certificate must be kept in the vehicle, but there is no requirement to carry the compulsory automobile liability insurance certificate or mutual-aid certificate.
questions.question_ja: 自動車を運転するときは、有効な自動車検査証を自動車に備えておかなければならないが、自動車損害賠償責任保険証明書や責任共済証明書は、備え付けが義務づけられていない。
questions.explanation: False. The required compulsory automobile liability insurance certificate or equivalent proof must also be kept as required; the inspection certificate alone is not sufficient.

questions.question_en: When a police officer at an intersection gives a hand signal with both arms raised vertically, traffic parallel to the front of the officer’s body is facing the equivalent of a yellow light.
questions.question_ja: 警察官が交差点で手信号により両腕を垂直に上げているときは、警察官の身体の正面に平行する交通に対しては、黄色の灯火の信号と同じである。
questions.explanation: True. For that direction of traffic, the officer’s raised-arm posture has the same effect as a yellow traffic signal.

questions.question_en: When starting a vehicle, you must signal your intention to start and then check the front, rear, left, and right again with mirrors and other means.
questions.question_ja: 車を発進させるときは、発進の合図をし、もう一度バックミラーなどで前後左右の安全を確かめなければならない
questions.explanation: True. A final safety check after signalling helps ensure that no road user has entered the vehicle’s path before it moves.

questions.question_en: Where the sidewalk and roadway are separated, goods may be displayed on the sidewalk.
questions.question_ja: 歩道と車道が区分されているところでは、歩道上に商品などを陳列してもよい。
questions.explanation: False. The sidewalk is for pedestrian passage and must not be obstructed by goods or other items in a way that interferes with traffic.

questions.question_en: On a one-way road, if an emergency vehicle approaches and moving to the left would instead obstruct it, you must move to the right.
questions.question_ja: 一方通行の道路で緊急自動車が接近してきたとき、左側に寄るとかえって緊急自動車の妨げになるようなときは、右側に寄らなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. On a one-way road, moving right is permitted and required when that is the direction that best clears a path for the emergency vehicle.

questions.question_en: Drivers should respect the position of pedestrians and other drivers and drive with consideration for them.
questions.question_ja: 運転者は、歩行者やほかの運転者の立場を尊重し、思いやりの気持ちを持つことが大切である。
questions.explanation: True. Safe driving requires not only technical rule compliance but also consideration for other road users.

questions.question_en: Before starting the engine of an automatic car, it is good to press the brake pedal to confirm its position and visually confirm the position of the accelerator pedal.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車は、エンジンを始動する前に、ブレーキペダルを踏んでその位置を確認し、アクセルペダルの位置を目で確認するのがよい。
questions.explanation: True. Confirming pedal positions before starting helps prevent pedal-selection mistakes and unintended acceleration.

questions.question_en: When turning left at an intersection, except a roundabout, watch carefully for motorcycles travelling along the left side, move close to the left edge in advance, and turn slowly so as not to cause a left-turn side-swipe accident.
questions.question_ja: 交差点（環状交差点を除く）を左折するときは、左側に寄って通行する二輪車に十分注意し、あらかじめ道路の左端に寄り、徐行しながら巻き込み事故を起こさないよう運転する。
questions.explanation: True. Moving left in advance and checking the left side reduces the risk of trapping a bicycle or motorcycle between the vehicle and the curb during the turn.

questions.question_en: If it is unavoidable to place a young child in the front passenger seat of a vehicle equipped with a passenger airbag, it is important to move the seat as far forward as possible before using the child seat.
questions.question_ja: 助手席にエアバッグを備えている自動車の助手席にやむを得ず幼児を同乗させるときは、座席をできるだけ前に出した上でチャイルドシートを使用させることが大切である。
questions.explanation: False. If a child must be placed in a front seat with an airbag, the seat should be moved as far back as practicable, not forward, to increase distance from the airbag.

questions.question_en: Automatic cars differ from manual cars in some operating methods, and not understanding those differences can cause an unexpected accident.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車は、マニュアル車と運転の方法が違うところがあり、それを知らないと思いがけない事故を起こすことがある。
questions.explanation: True. Features such as creep, selector positions, and accelerator response require correct automatic-transmission handling.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates a bicycle-only road.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、自転車専用道路であることを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured five-sided sign indicates a bicycle crossing, not a bicycle-only road.

questions.question_en: When traffic lanes are divided by a yellow line, you must not cross the yellow line to change lanes even for a right or left turn.
questions.question_ja: 車両通行帯が黄の線で区画されているときは、右折や左折のためでも黄の線をこえて進路を変えてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A yellow lane boundary prohibits crossing it for a lane or course change; a planned turn does not cancel that restriction.

questions.question_en: Automatic cars are easier to operate because there is no clutch operation, but careless driving can still involve unexpected dangers, so correct operation is important.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車は、クラッチ操作がいらないので負担が軽く運転は楽であるが、安易な気持ちで運転すると思いがけない危険がひそんでいるので、正しい運転操作をすることが大切である。
questions.explanation: True. Simpler controls do not remove the risks of incorrect selector, brake, or accelerator operation.

questions.question_en: When an ordinary motor vehicle tows a vehicle with a gross weight of 750 kilograms or less, a towing license is required in addition to the license for the towing vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 普通自動車で車両総重量が750キログラム以下の車をけん引するときは、けん引する自動車の免許のほかにけん引免許が必要である。
questions.explanation: False. A separate towing license is generally not required when the gross weight of the towed vehicle is 750 kilograms or less.

questions.question_en: On a road with three lanes in the same direction, as long as the rightmost lane is kept open for overtaking, you may use either of the other lanes regardless of your vehicle’s speed.
questions.question_ja: 同一方向に三つの車線がある道路では、最も右側の車線を追越しのためにあけておけば、車の速度に関係なくそのほかのどの車線を通行してもよい。
questions.explanation: False. On a multi-lane road, lane use is not completely optional; slower vehicles should generally use lanes farther to the left, while the rightmost lane is ordinarily kept for overtaking.

questions.question_en: I had been drinking, but because it was late at night and there were few people on the road, I drove carefully.
questions.question_ja: 飲酒したが、深夜であるため人通りも少ない道路であったので、気をつけて自動車を運転した。
questions.explanation: False. Light traffic or careful driving does not make driving after drinking permissible.

questions.question_en: This sign means there are many pedestrians ahead, so vehicles must proceed with caution.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先は歩行者が多いので、車両は注意して通行しなければならないことを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured blue circular sign designates a pedestrian-only road or area; it is not merely a warning that many pedestrians are ahead.

questions.question_en: For a long drive, it is good to plan the route, expected travel time, and rest locations in advance, and if you become sleepy, promptly rest until the drowsiness clears before driving again.
questions.question_ja: 長距離の運転をするときは、あらかじめ、運転コース、所要時間、休息場所を計画し、眠気を感じたらすみやかに休息をとって眠気を覚ましてから運転するとよい。
questions.explanation: True. Planned breaks and stopping when drowsy are basic measures for preventing fatigue-related crashes.

questions.question_en: A moped license allows you to drive a small special vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 原付免許で小型特殊自動車の運転をすることができる。
questions.explanation: False. A moped license does not include the privilege to drive a small special vehicle.

questions.question_en: On a moped, I wanted to shop at a supermarket on the right side of the road, so I crossed immediately in front of an approaching oncoming vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 原動機付自転車で、進行方向の右側の道路に面したスーパーマーケットで買い物をするため、走行してくる対向車の直前を横断した
questions.explanation: False. Crossing in front of an approaching vehicle without sufficient safe distance is dangerous and must not be done.

questions.question_en: When driving around a road corner or curve, you must be careful because vehicle off-tracking can cause the rear wheels to run onto the road shoulder.
questions.question_ja: 道路の曲がり角やカーブを走行するときは、車の内輪差により後輪が路肩にはみ出すおそれがあるので注意しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Rear wheels follow a path inside that of the front wheels during a turn, so the driver must allow for off-tracking.

questions.question_en: A motor vehicle must not overtake the vehicle ahead when that vehicle is about to move to the right to turn right or for a similar reason.
questions.question_ja: 自動車は、前の車が右折などのために右側に進路を変えようとしているときは、これを追越してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. Overtaking a vehicle that is signalling or positioning to move right creates a direct conflict with its intended path.

questions.question_en: Before getting into a vehicle, it is important to check that there is nobody in front of or behind it and that no child is underneath it.
questions.question_ja: 車に乗る前に、車の前後に人がいないか、車の下にこどもがいないかを確かめることが大切である。
questions.explanation: True. A walk-around check can reveal people, especially small children, who are in areas the driver may not see from the seat.

questions.question_en: Overtaking is prohibited on a steep downhill slope, but a slow large truck was ahead, so I overtook it.
questions.question_ja: こう配の急な下り坂では追越しをしてはならないが、前方を速度の遅い大型トラックが走っていたので追越した。
questions.explanation: False. A slow vehicle ahead does not remove the overtaking prohibition on a steep downhill slope.

questions.question_en: The load on a large truck ahead looked likely to collapse, so I kept a large following distance.
questions.question_ja: 前を走行中の大型貨物自動車の積み荷が荷くずれを起こしそうだったので、十分な車間距離をとって走行した。
questions.explanation: True. Extra distance reduces the risk from falling cargo and gives more time to react.

questions.question_en: When overtaking a motor vehicle or moped, a vehicle must normally pass on its right side.
questions.question_ja: 車は、自動車や原動機付自転車を追越すとき、その右側を通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The basic overtaking method is to pass to the right of the vehicle being overtaken, subject to the specific exceptions and restrictions in the rules.

questions.question_en: The police officer’s hand signal shown has the same meaning as a red traffic light for traffic travelling in the direction of the arrow.
questions.question_ja: この図のような警察官の手信号は、矢印の方向に対しては、信号機の赤色の灯火の信号と同じ意味である。
questions.explanation: True. For the direction indicated in the illustration, the officer’s posture requires traffic to stop as it would for a red light.

questions.question_en: When making an emergency stop in a vehicle equipped with an anti-lock braking system, you must press the brake pedal gradually in order to activate the system.
questions.question_ja: アンチロックブレーキシステムを備えた自動車で急ブレーキをかける場合は、システムを有効にするため、ゆっくり踏み込むことが必要である。
questions.explanation: False. In an emergency with ABS, the brake pedal should be pressed firmly and continuously; the system automatically prevents wheel lock.

questions.question_en: I overtook a large truck inside a tunnel that has traffic lanes.
questions.question_ja: 車両通行帯のあるトンネル内で、大型貨物自動車を追越した。
questions.explanation: True. A tunnel with marked traffic lanes is not subject to the general tunnel overtaking ban solely because it is a tunnel, unless another restriction applies.

questions.question_en: A push-button railway-crossing obstruction warning device should be used only when no flare or similar warning device is available.
questions.question_ja: 押しボタン式の踏切支障報知装置（非常ボタン）は発炎筒などがない場合以外は用いるべきではない。
questions.explanation: False. If a vehicle is stranded or another emergency obstructs the crossing, the emergency warning button should be used promptly when available; it is not merely a last resort after other devices.

questions.question_en: A light vehicle facing this signal may proceed in the direction of the arrow.
questions.question_ja: この信号に対面する軽車両は、矢印の方向に進行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. The illustration shows a red signal with a right-pointing green arrow. A light vehicle such as a bicycle is not permitted to make that right turn solely on this arrow.

questions.question_en: An emergency vehicle approached near an intersection, so I moved to the left side of the intersection and gave way.
questions.question_ja: 交差点の付近で緊急自動車が近づいてきたので、交差点の左側に寄って進路をゆずった。
questions.explanation: False. Near an intersection, a driver should avoid entering the intersection, move to the left side of the road, and stop to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.

questions.question_en: While overtaking, you must maintain a safe lateral distance from the vehicle you are passing.
questions.question_ja: 追越し中は、追越す車との間に安全な間隔を保たなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Adequate side clearance is necessary throughout the overtaking manoeuvre to prevent contact or destabilization.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that two-wheeled vehicles are prohibited from using the road.
questions.question_ja: この標識のある道路は、二輪車は通行することができないことを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured sign prohibits carrying a passenger on a motorcycle; it does not prohibit motorcycles themselves from using the road.

questions.question_en: Even near a kindergarten, if there is no school-route sign there is little need to watch for children suddenly running into the road.
questions.question_ja: 幼稚園の近くでも通学路の標識がなければ、こどもの飛び出しにそれほど注意する必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. The absence of a school-route sign does not remove the predictable risk of children near a kindergarten.

questions.question_en: At an uncontrolled intersection where the roads are about the same width, except a roundabout, you must not obstruct a streetcar or a vehicle approaching from the left.
questions.question_ja: 交通整理の行われていない、道路幅が同じような交差点（環状交差点を除く）では、路面電車や左方からくる車の進行を妨げてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. Streetcars and vehicles having the applicable left-side priority must be allowed to proceed without obstruction.

questions.question_en: At a signal-controlled intersection with no stop line, the stopping position is immediately before the traffic signal.
questions.question_ja: 信号機のある交差点で、停止線のないときの停止位置は、信号機の直前である。
questions.explanation: False. When there is no stop line, the required stopping position is determined in relation to the intersection or crossing, not simply directly beneath or before the signal itself.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that the road ahead is a dead end.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、道路がこの先で行き止まりになっていることを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured warning sign indicates that the road becomes narrower ahead, not that it ends.

questions.question_en: At a stop with a safety island, if nobody is in the safety island you do not have to slow down.
questions.question_ja: 安全地帯のある停留所で、人がいないときは徐行しなくてもよい。
questions.explanation: True as the source question is framed. With no person present at the safety island, the statement is treated as permitting normal passage; separate rules apply if a streetcar is stopped or passengers are boarding or alighting.

questions.question_en: When parking an automatic car and leaving it for a short time, applying the parking brake is enough, so the selector may be left in “D.”
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車を駐車させて、短時間、車から離れるときは、ハンドブレーキさえかけておけば、チェンジレバーが「D」（前進）であってもよい。
questions.explanation: False. When parking and leaving an automatic car, it should be secured and the selector placed in P; leaving it in D risks unintended movement.

questions.question_en: A license suspension or provisional suspension is different from revocation, so during the suspension period you may drive when necessary.
questions.question_ja: 免許の停止、仮停止処分は取消処分と違うので、その期間中であっても、必要なときは運転してもよい。
questions.explanation: False. Driving privileges are unavailable during a suspension period; necessity does not make driving lawful.

questions.question_en: A person who has held an ordinary license for less than one year does not need to display the beginner-driver mark when driving an ordinary car borrowed from someone else.
questions.question_ja: 普通免許を受けてから1年を経過していない者は、ほかの人から普通自動車を借りて運転する場合は、「初心者マーク」をつけなくてもよい。
questions.explanation: False. The beginner-mark requirement is based on the novice driver and applicable vehicle, not on who owns the car.

questions.question_en: When the road is wet and the tires are worn, stopping distance can be about twice as long as on a dry road with tires in good condition.
questions.question_ja: 路面が雨にぬれ、タイヤがすり減っている場合の停止距離は、乾燥した路面でタイヤの状態がよい場合に比べて、2倍程度長くなることがある。
questions.explanation: True. Reduced tire grip and a wet surface can substantially lengthen braking distance.

questions.question_en: This sign means you must not proceed in any direction other than the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、矢印の方向以外に進んではならないことを表している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured mandatory-direction sign restricts vehicles to the indicated direction or directions.

questions.question_en: Proceeding slowly means travelling at no more than one-half of the maximum speed shown by a sign or marking.
questions.question_ja: 徐行とは、標識や標示によって示されている最高速度の2分の1以下の速度で進むことである。
questions.explanation: False. “Proceed slowly” means travelling at a speed at which the vehicle can stop immediately; it is not defined as one-half of the posted maximum speed.

questions.question_en: Driving without causing inconvenience to others or making them feel endangered is also a basic part of safe driving.
questions.question_ja: 他人に迷惑をかけたり、危険を感じさせたりすることのない運転も安全運転の基本である。
questions.explanation: True. Safe driving requires considerate and predictable behaviour in addition to formal rule compliance.

questions.question_en: At an unsignalized intersection, I saw a pedestrian begin crossing at a pedestrian crossing. The pedestrian stopped after seeing my car, so I slowed down and passed without stopping.
questions.question_ja: 信号のない交差点を直進しようとしたところ横断歩道を渡り始めた歩行者を認めたが、自分の運転する車を見て立ち止まったので、一時停止せずに徐行して通過した。
questions.explanation: False. A pedestrian who is crossing or about to cross at a pedestrian crossing has priority; the driver must stop and yield rather than rely on the pedestrian stopping.

questions.question_en: When passing beside a bicycle, you need to take precautions such as leaving a safe distance from the bicycle or proceeding slowly.
questions.question_ja: 自転車のそばを通るときは、自転車との間に安全な間隔をあけるか、徐行するなどの注意が必要である。
questions.explanation: True. Adequate lateral clearance or sufficiently slow speed is required to protect the cyclist during a close pass.

questions.question_en: Seat belts can greatly reduce injury in a traffic accident.
questions.question_ja: シートベルトは、交通事故にあった場合の被害を大幅に軽減する効果がある。
questions.explanation: True. A correctly worn seat belt restrains the occupant and substantially reduces the risk and severity of impact injuries.

questions.question_en: Braking distance is the distance travelled from the time the brakes begin to take effect until the vehicle stops.
questions.question_ja: 制動距離とは、車のブレーキがきき始めてから、車が停止するまでの距離をいう。
questions.explanation: True. That is the definition of braking distance; it does not include the reaction distance before effective braking begins.

questions.question_en: A truck was stopped ahead. I saw a child run from the sidewalk in front of the truck, so I stopped before passing beside the truck.
questions.question_ja: 前方にトラックが止まっていたが、左側の歩道からそのトラックの前に駆け込んだこどもを認めたので、そのトラックのそばを通過する手前で一時停止した。
questions.explanation: True. The stopped truck creates a blind area, and stopping before passing it is an appropriate response to the visible child and possible additional hazards.

questions.question_en: When a vehicle crosses a sidewalk or roadside strip to enter or leave a place facing the road, it does not need to stop immediately before crossing if there are no pedestrians.
questions.question_ja: 車は、道路に面した場所に出入りするため歩道や路側帯を横切る場合に、歩行者がいなければその直前で一時停止する必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. The vehicle must stop immediately before crossing the sidewalk or roadside strip even when no pedestrian is visible.

questions.question_en: Immediately after starting an automatic car’s engine or while the air conditioner is operating, engine speed is low, so you should press the accelerator more strongly.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車で、エンジン始動直後やエアコン作動時は、エンジンの回転数が低くなっているので、アクセルペダルを強く踏むようにする。
questions.explanation: False. Engine speed can be higher after startup or when auxiliary loads operate; pressing the accelerator strongly can cause unintended rapid movement.

questions.question_en: A vehicle’s blind spots are generally larger on a large vehicle than on a small vehicle and on a cargo vehicle than on a passenger car, and cargo can enlarge or change them further.
questions.question_ja: 車の死角は、一般に小型車より大型車、乗用車より貨物車の方が大きくなり、また貨物を積んでいるときは更にその積載物により影響される。
questions.explanation: True. Vehicle size, body shape, and the load can obstruct more of the driver’s view.

questions.question_en: When driving, it is dangerous to rest your elbow on the window frame, so it is better not to do so.
questions.question_ja: 車を運転するときに、ひじを窓わくにのせて運転するのは、危険なのでやめた方がよい。
questions.explanation: True. A relaxed one-handed posture can reduce steering control and delay an emergency response.

questions.question_en: If you unavoidably need to use a mobile phone while driving, you should stop the vehicle in a safe place before using it.
questions.question_ja: 車を運転中、やむを得ず携帯電話を使用する必要が生じたときは、できるだけ安全な場所に車を止めて使用するとよい。
questions.explanation: True. Stopping safely removes the distraction from active driving and avoids prohibited handheld use while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question_en: The driver’s hand signal shown means that the vehicle will slow down or stop.
questions.question_ja: 図のような運転者の手による合図は、徐行か停止をするときの合図である。
questions.explanation: False. The illustrated raised-arm hand signal indicates a left turn; the hand signal for slowing or stopping uses a different arm position.

questions.question_en: After completing a turn or similar manoeuvre, promptly cancel the signal, and do not give unnecessary signals.
questions.question_ja: 右左折などの行為が終わった後は速やかに合図を戻し、また、不必要な合図をしてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A signal left on after the manoeuvre can mislead other road users and create danger.

questions.question_en: Even if the traffic light ahead is red, if a police officer controlling traffic directs you to turn right or left, you must follow the officer’s direction.
questions.question_ja: 前方の信号機の信号が赤でも、交通整理中の警察官が右折や左折の指示をしたときは、それに従わなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A police officer’s traffic instruction takes precedence over the traffic light.

questions.question_en: Within a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing and the 30 meters before it, overtaking another vehicle, excluding light vehicles, is prohibited, but passing it without an overtaking manoeuvre is not prohibited.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道や自転車横断帯とその手前から30メートル以内の場所では、ほかの車（軽車両を除く）を追越すことは禁止されているが、追抜くことは禁止されていない。
questions.explanation: False. The rule also prohibits passing alongside a vehicle and moving ahead of it in this protected crossing zone; it is not limited only to formal overtaking.

questions.question_en: At a signal-controlled intersection with a stop line, the stopping position is immediately before the stop line.
questions.question_ja: 停止線がある信号交差点での停止位置は、その停止線の直前である。
questions.explanation: True. When a stop line is provided, it defines where a vehicle must stop for the signal.

questions.question_en: After getting into a car, you should close the door forcefully in one continuous motion without pausing so that it does not remain partly open.
questions.question_ja: 自動車に乗ってからドアを閉めるときは、半ドアを防ぐため、力強く、途中で止めないで一気に閉めるようにする。
questions.explanation: False. The door should first be brought nearly closed while checking that clothing, fingers, and surrounding people are clear, then closed securely; slamming it blindly can cause injury.

questions.question_en: When preparing to turn left at the intersection ahead, except a roundabout, you should consider vehicles travelling on the left, move toward the center of the road, and then turn left slowly.
questions.question_ja: 前方の交差点（環状交差点を除く）を左折しようとするときは、左側を通行する車の安全を考え、道路の中央に寄ってから徐行して左折する。
questions.explanation: False. For a left turn, you should move close to the left edge in advance and turn slowly while checking for bicycles and motorcycles on the left.

questions.question_en: At a place with this sign, vehicles are prohibited from crossing the road, except a crossing involving a left turn to enter or leave a facility or place outside the road.
questions.question_ja: この標識のあるところでは、車の横断（道路外の施設または場所に出入りするための左折を伴う横断を除く）を禁止している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured regulatory sign prohibits the specified vehicle-crossing movement, subject to the exception stated in the question.

questions.question_en: Even if you hold a license, driving during a license suspension or provisional suspension is treated as unlicensed driving.
questions.question_ja: 免許を受けていても、免許の停止、仮停止期間中に運転すると無免許運転となる。
questions.explanation: True. A suspended license does not confer a current right to drive during the suspension period.

questions.question_en: When a vehicle with a lower maximum speed than yours is trying to overtake you, you must not increase speed, but you do not need to give way.
questions.question_ja: 自分の車より最高速度の低い車が追越そうとしているときは、速度を上げてはならないが、進路をゆずる必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. The vehicle being overtaken must not accelerate and, when necessary, must also keep left or otherwise provide sufficient room for the overtaking vehicle.

questions.question_en: When a school or kindergarten bus is stopped and children are getting on or off, if you pass beside it and move ahead you must proceed slowly and watch for children suddenly entering the road.
questions.question_ja: 通学・通園バスが止まっていて、園児などが乗り降りしているときに、その側方を通って前方に出ようとするときは、園児などの飛び出しに気をつけて徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Children may emerge unexpectedly from around the bus, so passing it requires especially slow and careful travel.

questions.question_en: In an emergency, it is acceptable to ask a person who has no driver’s license to drive the vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 緊急の際には、運転免許のない人に車の運転を頼んでも差しつかえない。
questions.explanation: False. An emergency does not generally authorize an unlicensed person to operate a vehicle.

questions.question_en: When traffic is congested, a police officer may give directions such as closing a road, and you must obey those directions.
questions.question_ja: 交通が混雑しているとき、警察官が通行止めなどの指示をすることがあるが、この場合はその指示に従わなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Lawful traffic directions given by police officers must be followed.

questions.question_en: When approaching a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing and it is not clear whether a pedestrian or bicycle is present, you must travel at a speed that allows you to stop before the crossing.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道や自転車横断帯に近づいたとき、歩行者や自転車がいるかいないか明らかでないときは、その手前で停止できるような速度で進まなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. If it is not clearly empty, the driver must be able to stop safely before the crossing.

questions.question_en: This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery and that you must be careful.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先の道路がすべりやすいので、注意しなければならないことを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured warning sign indicates a winding road ahead; it is not the slippery-road sign.

questions.question_en: If you continue riding a moped after forgetting to cancel the turn signal, other drivers may misunderstand your intention, so after each turn you should check that the signal has been cancelled.
questions.question_ja: 原動機付自転車で方向指示器の合図を戻し忘れたまま走行すると、ほかの車に誤解を与え危険を伴うことがあるので、右左折が終わったときは、そのつど戻し忘れがないかを確認することが必要である。
questions.explanation: True. A signal that remains on gives false information to other road users and can cause a collision.

questions.question_en: Correct seat-belt use includes positioning the lap belt around the pelvis and checking that the belt is not twisted.
questions.question_ja: シートベルトの正しい着用は腰ベルトは骨盤を巻くようにし、ベルトがねじれていないかどうかを確認する。
questions.explanation: True. A low, untwisted lap belt over the pelvis allows the restraint to distribute crash forces more safely.

questions.question_en: An elderly driver displaying the elderly-driver mark is not a beginner, so there is no need to protect that vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 高齢者マークをつけた高齢運転者は、初心運転者ではないので、保護する必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. Vehicles displaying the elderly-driver mark are specifically protected from unnecessary crowding and cutting in, even though the driver is not a beginner.

questions.question_en: When going straight through an intersection, except a roundabout, watch the movements of an oncoming right-turning vehicle because its driver may misjudge your speed or distance.
questions.question_ja: 交差点（環状交差点を除く）を直進するときは、対向の右折車が速度や距離を見誤ることがあるのでその動向に注意する。
questions.explanation: True. Right-turn conflicts often result from errors in judging an approaching vehicle’s speed and distance.

questions.question_en: Long-distance driving is tiring, so it is good to rest an elbow on the window frame or lean the body sideways while driving.
questions.question_ja: 長距離運転は疲れるので、ひじを窓わくにのせたり、体を斜めにして運転するとよい。
questions.explanation: False. A poor driving posture reduces steering control, observation, and the ability to respond quickly; fatigue should be managed with proper rest instead.

questions.question_en: You must proceed slowly near a road corner.
questions.question_ja: 道路の曲がり角付近を通行するときは徐行する。
questions.explanation: True. The area near a road corner is a designated location where a vehicle must slow down.

questions.question_en: While I was travelling inside an intersection, an emergency vehicle approached from behind, so I stopped immediately where I was.
questions.question_ja: 交差点内を進行中、後方から緊急自動車が接近してきたので、その場にただちに停止した。
questions.explanation: False. Stopping inside the intersection can obstruct the emergency vehicle and other traffic. You should clear the intersection first and then move aside appropriately.

questions.question_en: The time to give the signal for stopping is when you are about to stop.
questions.question_ja: 車が停止するときの合図の時期は、停止しようとするときである。
questions.explanation: True. The stopping signal is given in connection with the intended deceleration or stop so following traffic has warning.

questions.question_en: A beginner who has held an ordinary license for less than one year displays the beginner-driver mark at the designated positions at both the front and rear of the vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 普通免許を受けて1年を経過していない初心運転者は、車の前と後ろの定められた位置に初心者マークをつける。
questions.explanation: True. The mark is required at the prescribed front and rear positions for an eligible novice driver.

questions.question_en: With this sign, motor vehicles, mopeds, and light vehicles are all prohibited from passing.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、自動車はもちろん、原動機付自転車や軽車両も通行できない。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured road-closed-to-vehicles sign covers the vehicle categories stated in the question.

questions.question_en: A driver must always consider weather and road conditions and keep enough following distance to avoid a collision even if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.
questions.question_ja: 運転者は、常に天候や路面の状態を考え、前の車が急に止まっても追突しないような安全な車間距離をとらなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Safe following distance varies with speed, road grip, visibility, and the possibility of sudden braking ahead.

questions.question_en: When passing a pedestrian, a vehicle must either leave a safe distance from the pedestrian or proceed slowly.
questions.question_ja: 車は、歩行者のそばを通るときは、歩行者との間に安全な間隔をあけるか、徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. This protects the pedestrian from close passing where lateral clearance is limited.

questions.question_en: In an automatic car, operation is basically just the accelerator and brake pedals, so there is no particular need to pay attention to selector-lever operation.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車は、アクセルペダルとブレーキペダルの操作が基本となるので、チェンジレバーの操作については、特に注意する必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. Correct selector operation is essential; selecting the wrong range or moving the selector carelessly can cause unintended vehicle movement.

questions.question_en: Even at an intersection where a sign or marking requires a stop, if no other vehicle is present and there appears to be no danger, you do not need to stop.
questions.question_ja: 標識や標示によって一時停止が指定されている交差点でも、ほかに通行している車などがなく危険がない場合は、一時停止する必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. A stop sign or marking requires a complete stop regardless of whether other traffic is visible.

questions.question_en: Overtaking involves complicated vehicle control, so even a confident driver should avoid a forced or unsafe overtake.
questions.question_ja: 追越しは、運転操作が複雑になるので、運転に自信があっても無理な追越しはしないことが大切である。
questions.explanation: True. An overtake should only be attempted when there is sufficient visibility, distance, and space to complete it safely.

questions.question_en: On a narrow road, the vehicle ahead suddenly reversed toward me, so I sounded the horn to warn it in order to prevent danger.
questions.question_ja: 狭い道で、前の車が急に後退してきたので、危険防止のため警音器を鳴らして注意を与えた。
questions.explanation: True. The horn may be used when necessary to avoid an immediate danger, as in the situation described.

questions.question_en: This arrow signal is exclusively for route buses, so vehicles other than route buses cannot proceed in the direction of the arrow.
questions.question_ja: この矢印の信号は路線バス専用なので、路線バス以外は矢印の方向に進むことはできない。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured green arrow is a traffic signal governing permitted vehicle movement; it is not a route-bus-only signal.

questions.question_en: Even if a sign sets the maximum speed at 20 km/h, you may exceed that speed when traffic is light.
questions.question_ja: 標識などで、最高速度が時速20キロメートルと指定されていても、交通量の少ないときは、その速度をこえて運転してもよい。
questions.explanation: False. A maximum-speed restriction remains in force regardless of traffic volume.

questions.question_en: While stopped at a red signal, I remembered an urgent matter and used a handheld mobile phone. The signal turned green, so I started moving while continuing the call.
questions.question_ja: 信号待ちで停止中、急用を思い出したので携帯電話を手に持って使用していたが、対面する信号が青になったので、そのまま話をしながら発進した。
questions.explanation: False. Once the vehicle begins moving, continuing to hold and use the phone while driving is prohibited and dangerous.

questions.question_en: On a road with three traffic lanes in the same direction, I drove a large truck straddling two lanes because traffic was congested.
questions.question_ja: 同一方向に三つの車両通行帯のある道路で、大型貨物自動車を運転し、二つの通行帯にまたがって通行した。
questions.explanation: False. A vehicle should remain within its proper lane; congestion does not justify straddling two lanes.

questions.question_en: In this situation, a vehicle travelling in lane A may change into lane B.
questions.question_ja: この場面で、Aの車両通行帯を通行する車は、Bの車両通行帯へ進路を変えることができる
questions.explanation: False. The yellow lane boundary shown between A and B prohibits crossing it to change lanes.

questions.question_en: When passing close to a stopped car, you should anticipate that its door may suddenly open and check safety, slow down, or leave sufficient clearance.
questions.question_ja: 止まっている自動車のすぐ近くを通るときは、その車のドアが急に開くかもしれないことを予測して、安全を確かめたり、徐行したり、また、間隔を十分保ったりすることが必要である。
questions.explanation: True. A stopped vehicle can create a sudden door-opening hazard, so a driver should prepare for it before passing.

questions.question_en: When a driver is tired, it takes longer to recognize and judge danger, so the reaction distance becomes longer.
questions.question_ja: 運転者が疲れていると、危険を判断するまでに時間がかかるので、空走距離が長くなる。
questions.explanation: True. Fatigue delays the driver’s response, allowing the vehicle to travel farther before effective braking begins.

questions.question_en: This sign means that you must not sound the horn unnecessarily.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、みだりに警音器を鳴らしてはいけないことを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured sign is a horn-use sign requiring the horn to be sounded as prescribed; it is not a general reminder against unnecessary horn use.

questions.question_en: This sign means that a vehicle may go straight or turn left, but may not turn right.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、車が直進や左折することはできるが、右折することはできないことを表している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured mandatory-direction sign allows the indicated straight and left movements and excludes a right turn.

questions.question_en: To drive an emergency vehicle, in addition to the license required for that vehicle, special qualifications concerning age and driving experience are required.
questions.question_ja: 緊急自動車を運転する場合は、その車に応じた運転免許のほかに、運転経験年数や年齢について特別の資格が必要である。
questions.explanation: True. Emergency-vehicle drivers are subject to additional qualification requirements beyond merely holding the vehicle-class license.

questions.question_en: When a police officer waves a light horizontally as shown, traffic in the direction of the arrow has the same meaning as a green traffic signal.
questions.question_ja: このように灯火を横に振っているときは、矢印の方向の交通については信号機の青色と同じである。
questions.explanation: True. For the illustrated direction, the officer’s light signal permits traffic to proceed as a green signal would.

questions.question_en: Motor vehicles and mopeds must not travel on sidewalks or roadside strips, except when crossing them to enter or leave a place facing the road.
questions.question_ja: 自動車も原動機付自転車も、道路に面した場所に出入りするために横切る場合のほかは、歩道や路側帯を通行してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. These areas are not normal travel lanes for motor vehicles or mopeds; only limited crossing for access is permitted.

questions.question_en: Immediately after starting an automatic car’s engine, engine speed can be high, so if the brake pedal is not held firmly the vehicle may move off suddenly.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車のエンジン始動直後は、回転数が高いので、ブレーキペダルをしっかり踏んで操作しないと急発進する危険性がある。
questions.explanation: True. Higher engine speed can strengthen creep or initial movement, making firm brake control important.

questions.question_en: With a first-class ordinary license, you cannot drive a taxi even merely to transfer it to a repair shop.
questions.question_ja: 第一種普通免許で、タクシーを修理工場まで回送するためでも運転することができない。
questions.explanation: False. A second-class license is required for carrying passengers commercially, but a first-class ordinary license can be sufficient to drive an ordinary taxi when no passenger transport service is being performed, such as moving it for repair.

questions.question_en: A four-wheeled vehicle driver should lock the doors and make sure passengers do not carelessly open a door.
questions.question_ja: 四輪車の運転者は、ドアをロックし、同乗者が不用意にドアを開けたりしないように注意しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The driver should help prevent passengers from opening a door into passing traffic or otherwise creating danger.

questions.question_en: My lane was heavily congested, so I considered it unavoidable and drove in a bus-exclusive lane.
questions.question_ja: 通行しているレーンの交通量が多く混雑していたので、やむを得ない場合であると思いバス専用レーンを通行した。
questions.explanation: False. Ordinary congestion does not authorize a vehicle that is not permitted in a bus-exclusive lane to use that lane.

questions.question_en: This signboard indicates that, in the direction of the arrow, there is a time-limited parking zone with parking meters.
questions.question_ja: この標示板は、矢印の方向にパーキング・メーターのある、時間制限駐車区間があることを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured sign gives the direction to the regulated parking area equipped with parking meters.

questions.question_en: When turning right at an intersection, except a roundabout, if a vehicle or streetcar is going straight or turning left, you must not obstruct it even if your vehicle entered the intersection first.
questions.question_ja: 交差点（環状交差点を除く）で右折しようとする場合に、その交差点で直進か左折をする車や路面電車があるときは、自分の車が先に交差点に入っていても、その進行を妨げてはいけない。
questions.explanation: True. A right-turning vehicle must yield to conflicting straight-through or left-turning traffic as required; entering first does not create priority.

questions.question_en: A vehicle must not overtake another vehicle, excluding light vehicles, at a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing or within 30 meters before it.
questions.question_ja: 車は、横断歩道や自転車横断帯とその手前から30メートル以内の場所では、ほかの車（軽車両を除く）を追越してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. These crossings and their 30-meter approach zones are protected from overtaking.

questions.question_en: When turning left at an intersection, it is safer to steer right first and then turn left because that reduces the effect of off-tracking.
questions.question_ja: 交差点を左折するときは、いったん右にハンドルを切ってから左折した方が、内輪差の影響が小さくなり安全である。
questions.explanation: False. Swinging right before a left turn creates additional conflicts and does not eliminate off-tracking; the safe method is to move left in advance and turn slowly.

questions.question_en: It is acceptable to overtake a moped on a steep downhill slope or near the crest of an uphill slope.
questions.question_ja: こう配の急な下り坂や上り坂の頂上付近では、原動機付自転車を追越してもよい。
questions.explanation: False. The overtaking prohibition at those dangerous locations also applies when the vehicle ahead is a moped.

questions.question_en: If a manual car stalls on a railway crossing, first calmly try restarting the engine; if that fails, as an emergency measure the vehicle may be moved with the starter motor in first or second gear.
questions.question_ja: 踏切内でエンストしたとき、マニュアル車では、あせらずエンジンをかけ直し、それでもダメなときは非常手段としてギアをローかセコンド（セカンド）に入れ、セルモータで動かすことができる。
questions.explanation: True as the source describes the emergency procedure for a vehicle on which the starter can move the car. The immediate objective is to clear the tracks and warn railway traffic if the vehicle cannot be moved.

questions.question_en: When a pedestrian is trying to cross the road where there is no pedestrian crossing, it is good to slow down or stop and give way.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道のないところで、歩行者が道路を渡ろうとしているときは、徐行か一時停止をして道をゆずると良い。
questions.explanation: True. Reducing speed or stopping to let the pedestrian cross is a safe way to avoid conflict and protect the pedestrian.

questions.question_en: After overtaking and before moving back in front of the overtaken vehicle, signal left, continue until the overtaken vehicle can be seen in the rear-view mirror, check safety, and then move gradually to the left.
questions.question_ja: 追越した後で、その車の前方に出るときは、左側の方向指示器を出し、追越した車がルームミラーで見えるくらいの距離までそのまま進み、安全を確認した後、進路をゆるやかに左にとるのがよい。
questions.explanation: True. Waiting until there is sufficient distance before returning to the lane prevents cutting in too closely in front of the overtaken vehicle.

questions.question_en: Before changing course, you must first check that it is safe behind you and then give the signal.
questions.question_ja: 進路変更をしようとするときは、あらかじめ後方の安全を確認してから合図をしなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Safety must be checked before signalling and the manoeuvre must be made only when surrounding traffic can accommodate the change.

questions.question_en: The intersection signal changed to yellow. I could have stopped safely, but because I thought it was acceptable as long as I could clear the intersection before red, I continued through carefully.
questions.question_ja: 交差点の信号機の信号が黄色に変わったとき、安全に停止できる状態であったが、赤になるまでに交差点を通過できればよいので、注意しながら通過した。
questions.explanation: False. When the signal turns yellow, a driver who can stop safely before the stopping position must stop rather than enter the intersection.

questions.question_en: On an ordinary road, if no traffic sign or marking specifies a maximum speed, a motor vehicle must not exceed 60 km/h.
questions.question_ja: 一般道路で自動車を運転するとき、最高速度が標識などで指定されていない場合は、時速60キロメートルをこえて運転してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. The general statutory maximum for the ordinary motor vehicles covered by this question is 60 km/h on ordinary roads unless another limit is specified.

questions.question_en: It is acceptable to ask a driver to operate an overloaded vehicle, or to sell or hand over goods in a way that causes overloading.
questions.question_ja: 運転者に過積載をして車を運転することを求めたり、過積載となるようなものを売り渡したり、引き渡したりしても構わない。
questions.explanation: False. Causing or encouraging overloading is prohibited; responsibility is not limited only to the person actually driving the overloaded vehicle.

questions.question_en: A motor vehicle must not overtake a motor vehicle or moped at a railway crossing or within 30 meters before it.
questions.question_ja: 踏切とその手前から30メートル以内の場所では、自動車や原動機付自転車を追越してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. Railway crossings and the 30-meter approach are overtaking-prohibited areas.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates a parking lot.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、駐車場であることを表している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured sign indicates an evacuation or refuge facility, not a parking area.

questions.question_en: When moving an automatic car’s selector into P, the vehicle should be completely stopped first; otherwise it can cause damage.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車のチェンジレバーをPに入れるときは、車が完全に停止してから入れないと故障の原因になる。
questions.explanation: True. P mechanically locks the transmission, so engaging it while the vehicle is still moving can damage the parking mechanism.

questions.question_en: At an intersection, if the signal facing your direction is flashing yellow, you must always come to a complete stop.
questions.question_ja: 交差点において、進行方向の信号が黄色の灯火の点滅をしている場合は、必ず一時停止しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. A flashing yellow signal requires proceeding with caution; it does not itself require a complete stop.

questions.question_en: Even when the vehicle ahead is overtaking another vehicle, if the road ahead is safe you may overtake both vehicles.
questions.question_ja: 前の車が自動車を追越そうとしているときであっても、前方の安全が確認できれば、さらに、これらの車を追越すことができる
questions.explanation: False. Beginning another overtake while the vehicle ahead is already overtaking creates a prohibited and highly dangerous multiple-overtaking situation.

questions.question_en: Near the crest of an uphill slope, a vehicle must proceed slowly.
questions.question_ja: 上り坂の頂上付近では、車は徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The road ahead cannot be seen sufficiently near a crest, so it is a designated slow-speed location.

questions.question_en: On a road where one side is a cliff with a risk of falling and two vehicles cannot pass safely, the vehicle on the cliff side should stop and give way.
questions.question_ja: 片側が転落するおそれがあるがけになっている道路で、安全に行き違うことができないときは、がけ側の車が一時停止して進路をゆずる。
questions.explanation: True. Giving the cliff-side vehicle room to remain stationary reduces the danger of being forced toward the edge during the passing manoeuvre.

questions.question_en: When overtaking the vehicle ahead, you must pass on its right, except when that vehicle has moved toward the road center, or toward the right edge on a one-way road, to turn right.
questions.question_ja: 前の車を追越すときは、前の車が右折のため道路の中央（一方通行の道路では右端）に寄って通行している場合を除き、その右側を通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Right-side passing is the normal overtaking method, while a vehicle positioned for a right turn is passed on the left when lawful and safe.

questions.question_en: When turning right from a one-way road, except at a roundabout, a motor vehicle must move close to the right edge and proceed slowly inside the center of the intersection.
questions.question_ja: 自動車が一方通行の道路から右折するとき（環状交差点を除く）は、道路の右端に寄り、交差点の中心の内側を徐行しながら通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A right turn from a one-way road begins from the right side and is made slowly through the proper part of the intersection.

questions.question_en: When passengers are getting on or off a streetcar, you must remain stopped until the passengers and people crossing the road are gone, regardless of whether a safety island is present.
questions.question_ja: 路面電車に乗り降りする人がいるときは、安全地帯の有無に関係なく、乗り降りする人や道路を横断する人がいなくなるまで停止していなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The rule differs depending on whether a safety island is present. With a safety island, a vehicle may pass the stopped streetcar slowly while protecting passengers; the blanket statement that stopping is always required regardless of the safety island is incorrect.

questions.question_en: When the vehicle ahead is signalling and moving toward the left edge or road center in order to leave the road, you must not obstruct its change of course except when necessary to avoid danger.
questions.question_ja: 前の車が道路外に出るため、道路の左端や中央に寄ろうとして、合図をしているときは、危険をさける場合を除いて、その進路の変更を妨げてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A vehicle that has properly signalled a lawful movement should be allowed to complete it unless giving way would create danger.

questions.question_en: When an automatic car is stopped at a signal or intersection, if the selector is in N there is absolutely no need to keep any brake applied.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車を運転中、交差点などで信号待ちのため停止したときは、チェンジレバーを「N」に入れておけば、ブレーキをかけておく必要は全くない。
questions.explanation: False. The vehicle must still be kept securely stopped; selecting N alone does not prevent it from rolling, especially on a slope.

questions.question_en: A bicycle was weaving from side to side on a wide road. Because I thought passing normally might cause contact, I sounded the horn to warn the cyclist.
questions.question_ja: 幅の広い道で、自転車が左右にふらつきながら通行していたので、そのまま追抜くと接触してしまうと思い、警音器を鳴らして注意をうながした。
questions.explanation: False. The safer response is to reduce speed and maintain adequate distance. The horn should not be used merely to pressure a cyclist unless it is genuinely necessary to avoid danger.

questions.question_en: Even at a signal-controlled intersection, a vehicle must proceed slowly when turning right or left.
questions.question_ja: 交通整理の行われている交差点を右折、左折するときでも徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The obligation to make a turn slowly applies even when the intersection is controlled by traffic signals.

questions.question_en: Driving at high speed shortens the time before reaching other vehicles, pedestrians, or obstacles, leaving less time and space to avoid an accident.
questions.question_ja: 速い速度での運転は、他車、歩行者、障害物などへの接近時間が短くなるため、事故を回避する余裕がなくなる。
questions.explanation: True. Higher speed reduces available reaction time and increases the distance required to slow or stop.

questions.question_en: Even when the road is wet from rain, if steering and braking are performed accurately, the same following distance as on a dry day is sufficient.
questions.question_ja: 雨などで路面がぬれていても、ハンドル操作やブレーキ操作を正確に行えば、車間距離は晴れの日と同じでよい。
questions.explanation: False. Wet roads reduce tire grip and can lengthen stopping distance, so a larger following distance is needed.

questions.question_en: At a marked no-stopping area in front of a fire station, you must not stop inside the marking, but at no-stopping markings in places other than fire stations you may stop.
questions.question_ja: 消防署の前にある停止禁止部分の標示があるところでは、標示部分に入って停止してはならないが、消防署以外の停止禁止部分の標示があるところでは停止してもよい。
questions.explanation: False. A designated no-stopping area prohibits stopping within the marked portion wherever that marking is lawfully installed.

questions.question_en: This sign prohibits all traffic, including vehicles and pedestrians.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、車はもちろん、歩行者などすべての通行の禁止を示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured sign prohibits vehicular traffic; it does not mean that every pedestrian is prohibited from passing.

questions.question_en: When an obstacle is in your lane ahead, it is best to accelerate sharply so you can pass it before an oncoming vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 進路の前方に障害物があるときは、対向車より先に通過するため、一気に加速して通過するとよい。
questions.explanation: False. The vehicle whose path is obstructed should slow or stop and yield as necessary rather than racing the oncoming vehicle for the available space.

questions.question_en: Good braking technique is to avoid unnecessary brake use and, where possible, gradually reduce speed by easing the accelerator before braking to a stop.
questions.question_ja: ブレーキの上手なかけ方は、むやみに使わないで、なるべくアクセルの操作で徐々に速度を落としてから止まるようにするとよい。
questions.explanation: True. Early, smooth deceleration reduces abrupt braking and gives following traffic more time to respond.

questions.question_en: While driving an ordinary passenger car on a road with a bus-priority lane, I used the priority lane in order to turn left.
questions.question_ja: 普通乗用車で走行中、路線バス等優先通行帯が設けられている道路で、優先通行帯を通行して左折した。
questions.explanation: True. A vehicle may enter the necessary portion of a bus-priority lane to make a lawful left turn, while still avoiding obstruction of buses.

questions.question_en: Where overtaking is prohibited by a sign, an ordinary car is also prohibited from overtaking a moped.
questions.question_ja: 標識により追越しが禁止されているところでは、普通自動車が原動機付自転車を追越すことも禁止されている。
questions.explanation: True. The overtaking prohibition includes overtaking a moped.

questions.question_en: It is a good idea to have a second driver’s license issued in advance in case the original is stolen or lost.
questions.question_ja: 運転免許証は、盗難や紛失に備えて、事前に再発行を受けておいた方がよい。
questions.explanation: False. Duplicate valid licenses are not issued simply as a spare; reissuance is obtained after a qualifying loss, theft, damage, or similar event.

questions.question_en: This sign means “left turn permitted.”
questions.question_ja: この標識は、「左折可」を表している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured rectangular blue arrow is a one-way indication showing the permitted direction of traffic; it is not the separate “left turn permitted” sign.

questions.question_en: When a four-wheeled vehicle turns left, the front and rear wheels follow the same path, so there is no risk of an accident caused by off-tracking.
questions.question_ja: 四輪車で左折するときは、前輪と後輪が同じところを通るので、内輪差によって生ずる事故は考えられない。
questions.explanation: False. The rear wheels travel inside the path of the front wheels during a turn, creating off-tracking and a risk to cyclists, pedestrians, or objects near the left side.

questions.question_en: You must not change course in a way that forces a vehicle approaching from behind to avoid you by sudden braking or sudden steering.
questions.question_ja: 後方から接近してくる自動車に急ブレーキや急ハンドルで避けさせるような方法で、その進路を変えてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A course change is prohibited when it would interfere with a following vehicle and force an abrupt evasive action.

questions.question_en: To drive a two-wheeled motor vehicle with an engine displacement over 50 cc, a large-motorcycle or ordinary-motorcycle license is required.
questions.question_ja: エンジンの総排気量が50ccをこえる二輪の自動車を運転するときは、大型二輪免許または普通二輪免許が必要である。
questions.explanation: True according to the source answer. The question treats a two-wheeled motor vehicle over 50 cc as requiring the appropriate motorcycle-license class rather than a moped license.

questions.question_en: When overtaking and crossing into the right side of the road, the amount by which the vehicle enters the right side should be kept as small as possible.
questions.question_ja: 追越しをするとき、進路を変え車体を道路の右側部分にはみ出す場合は、できるだけそのはみ出す部分を少なくするのがよい。
questions.explanation: True. Any permitted right-side encroachment for overtaking should be limited to the minimum needed to complete the manoeuvre safely.

questions.question_en: When carrying a child in a car, it is better to seat the child in the rear rather than the front seat.
questions.question_ja: こどもを車に乗せるときは、前部座席よりも後部座席に乗せた方がよい。
questions.explanation: True. The rear seat generally places a child farther from frontal impact forces and a front passenger airbag.

questions.question_en: When driving on a priority road, vehicles entering from intersecting roads will always stop, so there is no need to slow down or pay special attention at an intersection.
questions.question_ja: 優先道路を通行しているときは、優先道路と交差する道路から出てくる車は必ず停止するので、交差点であっても速度を落としたり、注意したりする必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. Priority does not guarantee that another driver will stop or notice you; you must still watch the intersection and adjust speed for safety.

questions.question_en: Compared with white road markings, yellow road markings can generally be understood as indicating a stronger restriction.
questions.question_ja: 白色の道路標示に比べると、黄色の道路標示の意味の方が、さらに強い制限を表していると考えてよい。
questions.explanation: True. In many common exam situations, yellow lines are used for restrictions such as prohibiting crossing a line, whereas a white line may only divide or guide traffic.

questions.question_en: Before starting a vehicle, it is necessary to check blind areas around the front, rear, and sides before getting in.
questions.question_ja: 車を発進させるときは、車に乗る前に車の前後、左右などの死角をよく確かめることが必要である。
questions.explanation: True. A pre-start walk-around can reveal children, objects, or other hazards that cannot be seen from the driving seat.

questions.question_en: When passing beside a school or kindergarten bus stopped for children to get on or off, you must always stop behind the bus and check safety.
questions.question_ja: 児童・幼児の乗り降りのため停止している通学・通園バスの側方を通過するときは、その後方で必ず一時停止して、安全を確かめなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The stated rule requires proceeding slowly and watching carefully for children; a complete stop is not automatically required in every such situation.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that the road curves to the left ahead.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、道路がこの先で左カーブになっていることを表している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured blue circular sign is a mandatory direction sign requiring a leftward movement; it is not a yellow warning sign for a left curve.

questions.question_en: Wearing a seat belt correctly helps maintain proper driving posture and can reduce fatigue while driving.
questions.question_ja: シートベルトを正しく着用すれば、運転姿勢が正しく保たれるため、運転中の疲労を軽減する。
questions.explanation: True. The belt supports a stable seating position and reduces unnecessary body movement while the vehicle is in motion.

questions.question_en: At an unsignalized intersection, I was going to turn left and saw a pedestrian crossing the road on the left-side pedestrian crossing, so I proceeded slowly immediately in front of the pedestrian.
questions.question_ja: 信号のない交差点を左折しようとしたところ、左方道路の横断歩道を渡っている歩行者を認めたので、徐行しながらその直前を通行した。
questions.explanation: False. A pedestrian using the crossing has priority; the driver must stop and must not pass in front in a way that obstructs the crossing.

questions.question_en: This road marking means “diagonal crossing permitted” and indicates that pedestrians may cross diagonally at the intersection.
questions.question_ja: この標示は、「斜め横断可」であり、歩行者が交差点で斜めに横断できることを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured marking designates an intersection where pedestrians may cross diagonally as indicated.

questions.question_en: When parking an automatic car, whether on an uphill or downhill slope, once the selector is in P there is no need to apply the parking brake.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車を駐車するときは、上り坂でも下り坂でもチェンジレバーをPに入れたら、ハンドブレーキをかける必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. The parking brake should be applied securely; P should not be relied on as the only means of holding the vehicle.

questions.question_en: A taxi was travelling in a lane marked for left turns at an intersection. A passenger signalled from straight ahead beyond the intersection, so the taxi continued straight through the intersection to pick up the passenger.
