questions.question_ja: タクシーの運転者が、標識や標示により、交差点で左折の進行方向が指定されている通行帯を通行中、交差点の前方で客が合図をしたので、そのまま交差点を直進して客を乗車させた。
questions.explanation: False. A vehicle in a lane whose direction is designated for left turns must follow that designated direction; seeking a passenger does not permit going straight.

questions.question_en: Only the “Stop” and “Slow” traffic signs use this shape.
questions.question_ja: この形の標識は、「一時停止」と「徐行」しかない。
questions.explanation: False. The inverted-triangle shape is also used for the sign indicating that the road ahead is a priority road, so it is not exclusive to those two signs.

questions.question_en: When passing beside a pedestrian or bicycle, you must slow down even when you can maintain a safe distance.
questions.question_ja: 車は、歩行者や自転車の側方を通過するとき、安全な間隔をあけることができても徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. If a sufficient safe lateral distance is maintained, slowing is not always required; when safe clearance cannot be maintained, slow travel is required.

questions.question_en: This sign warns of possible strong crosswinds ahead, so you should reduce speed as necessary and take care not to have the steering affected.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先の道路では強い横風の吹くおそれがあることを示しているので、減速するなどして、ハンドルが取られないように注意しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured crosswind warning sign indicates a place where sudden side winds can push the vehicle off its intended path.

questions.question_en: When entering a road with this sign, you must stop once and then proceed.
questions.question_ja: この標識がある道路に入るときは、一時停止してから通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured no-entry sign prohibits entering from that direction; stopping first does not make entry permissible.

questions.question_en: This road marking indicates a bicycle crossing.
questions.question_ja: この標示は、自転車横断帯を示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured bicycle-and-direction road marking is not the designated transverse marking for a bicycle crossing; it provides a different bicycle traffic-direction instruction.

questions.question_en: The purpose of requiring novice drivers to display the beginner-driver mark is to make them aware that they are beginners and encourage careful driving, while also requiring surrounding drivers to protect vehicles displaying the mark.
questions.question_ja: 初心運転者に初心者マークを表示させるのは、初心者であることを自覚させ、かつ慎重な運転をするように求めるとともに、周囲のドライバーにも初心者マークを表示した車両を保護させようとするためである。
questions.explanation: True. The mark both identifies a novice driver and creates protective duties for surrounding traffic, such as restrictions on unnecessary crowding or cutting in.

questions.question_en: At an intersection where a sign specifies permitted directions such as straight ahead or left turn, you must proceed only in the direction or directions specified.
questions.question_ja: 標識によって直進や左折など進行方向が指定されている交差点では、その指定された方向にしか進行してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A mandatory-direction sign controls the permitted movement at the intersection, so a driver must follow the indicated direction.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that motorcycles may use the road.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、自動二輪車が通行できることを表している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured sign prohibits the covered two-wheeled motor vehicles and mopeds; it does not indicate that motorcycles are permitted.

questions.question_en: When a police officer at an intersection holds both arms horizontally, traffic travelling parallel to the front of the officer’s body has the same meaning as a red traffic light.
questions.question_ja: 警察官が交差点で手信号により両腕を水平に上げているときは、警察官の身体の正面に平行する交通に対しては、信号機の赤色の灯火の信号と同じ意味である。
questions.explanation: False. With the officer’s arms held horizontally, traffic in that parallel direction is permitted to proceed; the statement incorrectly describes it as red.

questions.question_en: Near a bend on a steeply sloped road, where a “right-side traffic” marking is provided, a vehicle may travel into the part of the road to the right of the center.
questions.question_ja: 車は、こう配の急な道路の曲がり角付近で、「右側通行」の標示があるところでは、道路の中央から右の部分にはみ出して通行することができる。
questions.explanation: True. The designated right-side-traffic marking is an exception that permits use of the indicated right-side portion at that location.

questions.question_en: When turning right or left at an intersection, if the signal ahead is green there is no need to slow down.
questions.question_ja: 交差点を右左折するときは、前方の信号が青であれば徐行する必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. Right and left turns must still be made slowly and safely even when the traffic signal is green.

questions.question_en: On a road where no maximum speed is specified by a sign or marking, a driver may travel at any speed that the driver personally considers safe.
questions.question_ja: 最高速度が標識などで指定されていない道路では、運転者が安全と思う速度であれば、どのような速度で運転してもよい。
questions.explanation: False. Statutory maximum speeds still apply even where no speed-limit sign or marking is posted.

questions.question_en: This sign means that you must turn left regardless of the traffic signal ahead.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、前方の信号に関係なく、左折しなければならないことを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured sign designates the direction for the traffic lane, but the driver must still obey the traffic signal controlling the intersection.

questions.question_en: When congestion requires a long stop on an uphill or downhill slope, it is better to use the parking brake as much as practicable.
questions.question_ja: 上り坂や下り坂で、渋滞のため長い間停車しなければならないときは、できるだけハンドブレーキを利用した方がよい。
questions.explanation: True. The parking brake helps hold the vehicle securely and reduces the risk of rolling during a prolonged stop on a slope.

questions.question_en: When approaching a pedestrian crossing, you must slow down even when it is clearly apparent that no pedestrian is present.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道に近づいたとき、歩行者が明らかにいなくても徐行して通過しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. If it is clearly apparent that nobody will cross, the special requirement to approach at a speed that allows stopping does not apply.

questions.question_en: A provisional driving license is required when a person seeking a large, medium, semi-medium, or ordinary vehicle license drives for practice.
questions.question_ja: 仮運転免許は、大型自動車や中型自動車、準中型自動車または普通自動車の免許を受けようとする者が、練習のため運転する場合に必要な免許である。
questions.explanation: True. The provisional license allows the applicable practice driving before the full license is obtained, subject to the required conditions.

questions.question_en: When a motor vehicle turns right from a one-way road, except at a roundabout, it must move as close as possible to the right edge and proceed slowly immediately inside the center of the intersection.
questions.question_ja: 一方通行の道路から右折する（環状交差点を除く）自動車は、できるだけ道路の右端に寄り、交差点の中心の直近の内側を徐行しながら通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. From a one-way road the vehicle moves close to the right edge and passes inside the intersection center, but the rule does not say “immediately inside” the center. That wording applies to an ordinary right turn from a two-way road.

questions.question_en: When leaving a home garage and crossing a sidewalk to enter the roadway, you must stop immediately before the sidewalk and must not obstruct pedestrians.
questions.question_ja: 自宅の車庫内から歩道を横切って車道に出る場合は、歩道の直前で一時停止をするとともに歩行者の通行を妨げないようにしなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A vehicle crossing a sidewalk to enter the road must stop before crossing it and give pedestrian traffic priority.

questions.question_en: This is a “No Right Turn” sign.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、右折禁止の標識である。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured sign is the vehicle-crossing prohibition sign used for the movement shown; it is not the ordinary no-right-turn sign.

questions.question_en: Children riding bicycles generally obey traffic rules well, so when passing beside them you can proceed safely without slowing down.
questions.question_ja: 自転車に乗っているこどもは、交通法規をよく守るので、その側方を通行するときは、徐行しなくても安心して通ることができる。
questions.explanation: False. Children can make sudden or unpredictable movements, so a driver must leave safe clearance or slow down as necessary.

questions.question_en: A cargo vehicle with a maximum payload of 3,000 kilograms may be driven with an ordinary driver’s license.
questions.question_ja: 最大積載量3,000キログラムの貨物自動車は、普通免許で運転できる。
questions.explanation: False. A 3,000-kilogram maximum payload exceeds the vehicle limits of the current ordinary-license category covered by the question.

questions.question_en: This sign means that vehicles may proceed only in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、矢印の示す方向にだけ車が進むことができることを表している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured mandatory-direction sign restricts travel to the indicated direction.

questions.question_en: This signboard indicates a one-way road.
questions.question_ja: この標示板は、一方通行であることを表している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured white signboard with a blue left arrow is the “left turn permitted” indication, not a one-way sign.

questions.question_en: When rear visibility is poor, or when backing from a narrow road into a wide road is unavoidable, it is good to ask a passenger to help check the area behind.
questions.question_ja: 後方の見通しがよくない場所や狭い道路から広い道路に出るところで、やむを得ずバックで発進する場合、同乗者に後方の確認を手伝ってもらうとよい。
questions.explanation: True. A spotter can observe blind areas that the driver cannot see while reversing.

questions.question_en: Before changing lanes, you must check the intended direction and the rear, and then change course in a way that makes an approaching vehicle brake or steer suddenly.
questions.question_ja: 進路変更は、進路を変えようとする方向や後方の安全確認を行い、後方から接近してくる車に急ブレーキや急ハンドルをさせるような方法で進路変更しなくてはならない。
questions.explanation: False. A lane change must not force an approaching vehicle to brake or steer abruptly; if it would, the lane change must be delayed.

questions.question_en: This road marking indicates that parking is prohibited.
questions.question_ja: この標示は、駐車禁止を示している。
questions.explanation: True. The pictured broken yellow curb-side line is the road marking for a parking prohibition.

questions.question_en: When a driver senses danger and presses the brake, the distance from the point at which the brakes begin to work until the vehicle stops is called braking distance.
questions.question_ja: 運転者が危険を感じてブレーキを踏んだとき、ブレーキが効き始めてから停止するまでの距離を、制動距離という。
questions.explanation: True. Braking distance is measured from effective brake action to complete stop.

questions.question_en: While driving, a mobile-phone message arrived, so I stared at the display in order to read it.
questions.question_ja: 自動車を運転中、携帯電話のメールが着信したので、メールの内容を読むため画像を注視した。
questions.explanation: False. Looking continuously at a phone display while driving diverts attention from the road and is prohibited.

questions.question_en: While driving an ordinary passenger car in a bus-priority lane, a kindergarten bus approached from behind, but because it was not a route bus I stayed in the lane.
questions.question_ja: 路線バス等優先通行帯を普通乗用車で走行中、後方から通園バスが接近してきたが、路線バスではないので通行帯を変えることなくそのまま進行した。
questions.explanation: False. School and kindergarten buses can be included among the vehicles given priority by the applicable bus-priority-lane rule, so the ordinary car must leave the lane when required to avoid obstruction.

questions.question_en: On a long downhill slope, you should use the foot brake frequently and there is no need to select a lower gear, such as 2 or L (or 1) in an automatic car.
questions.question_ja: 長い下り坂では、ひんぱんにフットブレーキを使い、低速ギア（オートマチック車ではチェンジレバーを2かL（または1））に落とす必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. On a long descent, engine braking with an appropriate lower gear should be used so the foot brakes do not overheat from continuous or frequent use.

questions.question_en: When entering a road on the left without changing lanes beforehand, except at a roundabout, the time to give the signal is when you begin turning the steering wheel.
questions.question_ja: 同一方向に車線を変えないまま、続いて左方の道に入るとき（環状交差点を除く）の合図の時期は、ハンドルを切るときである。
questions.explanation: False. A left-turn signal should be given from about 30 meters before the turning point, not only when steering begins.

questions.question_en: To prevent a seat belt from coming undone, the buckle tongue must be inserted securely.
questions.question_ja: シートベルトがはずれないよう、バックルの金具は確実に差込まなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. The buckle must latch completely so the restraint remains fastened during normal travel and a collision.

questions.question_en: I thought it might interfere with driving, but I put a large pet dog in the front passenger seat and went for a drive.
questions.question_ja: 運転操作の妨げになると思ったが、ペットの大型犬を助手席に載せてドライブへ行った。
questions.explanation: False. An animal must not be carried where it can interfere with steering, pedals, visibility, or other driving operations.

questions.question_en: When following another vehicle through a right turn at an intersection, except a roundabout, you do not need to signal if the vehicle ahead is already signalling.
questions.question_ja: 前車に引き続き交差点（環状交差点を除く）を右折する場合、前車がすでに合図をしているときは、右折の合図をしなくてもよい。
questions.explanation: False. Each driver must give that driver’s own required turn signal; another vehicle’s signal does not substitute for it.

questions.question_en: When preparing to turn left at the intersection ahead, except a roundabout, you should leave as much space as possible on the left side for the safety of vehicles travelling there and turn slowly.
questions.question_ja: 前方の交差点（環状交差点を除く）を左折しようとするときは、左側を通行する車の安全を考え、道路の左側をできるだけあけて徐行しながら左折する。
questions.explanation: False. A left-turning vehicle should move close to the left edge in advance, while carefully checking for bicycles and motorcycles so they are not trapped alongside.

questions.question_en: I had a high fever from a cold and had taken cold medicine that causes drowsiness, but work was busy, so I drove to work.
questions.question_ja: かぜで高い熱が出て、睡眠作用のあるかぜ薬を服用していたが、会社の仕事が忙しかったので、車の運転をして出勤した。
questions.explanation: False. A driver must not drive when illness or medication impairs alertness or the ability to operate the vehicle safely.

questions.question_en: The prohibition against crowding alongside or cutting in applies only to vehicles displaying a provisional-license practice sign.
questions.question_ja: 幅寄せや割り込みが禁止されているのは、仮免許練習標識をつけた車に対してのみである。
questions.explanation: False. Similar protective rules apply to several designated marks, including beginner, elderly, disabled, and hearing-impaired driver marks, as applicable.

questions.question_en: Large and ordinary motorcycles may use a lane reserved exclusively for route buses whenever bus traffic is light.
questions.question_ja: 大型自動二輪車や普通自動二輪車は、路線バスなどの専用通行帯に指定されている道路では、路線バスなどの交通が少ないときは通行してもよい。
questions.explanation: False. Low bus traffic does not make a bus-exclusive lane open to an ordinary motorcycle that is not otherwise permitted to use it.

questions.question_en: Near a road corner, a vehicle can cross the center and collide with oncoming traffic, so overtaking a motor vehicle or moped is prohibited there.
questions.question_ja: 道路の曲がり角付近では、車が道路中央からはみ出たりして、前方から進行してくる車と衝突する危険性が高いので、自動車や原動機付自転車を追越してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. Limited visibility and the risk of crossing into opposing traffic make road corners overtaking-prohibited locations.

questions.question_en: When a pedestrian is crossing a pedestrian crossing, you must stop before the crossing, or before the stop line if one is present, and give way to the pedestrian.
questions.question_ja: 歩行者が横断歩道を横断しているときは、横断歩道の手前（停止線があるときは、その手前）で一時停止をして、歩行者に道をゆずらなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Pedestrians on or about to enter the crossing have priority, and the vehicle must stop without obstructing them.

questions.question_en: On a road without a separate sidewalk and roadway, when passing a pedestrian you must either keep a safe distance or proceed slowly.
questions.question_ja: 歩道と車道の区別のない道路で歩行者のそばを通るときは、歩行者との間に安全な間隔をあけるか、徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A driver must protect a nearby pedestrian through sufficient clearance or slow travel.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that traffic merges ahead.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先の道路が合流交通になっていることを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured yellow Y-shaped warning sign indicates a Y-shaped intersection or branch ahead, not merging traffic.

questions.question_en: When applying the brakes, it is good to press lightly at first and then gradually increase pressure to the strength needed.
questions.question_ja: ブレーキをかけるときは、最初はできるだけ軽く踏み込み、それから必要な強さまで徐々に踏み込むのがよい。
questions.explanation: True. Progressive braking gives smoother vehicle control and provides clearer warning to following traffic, except when an emergency requires immediate hard braking.

questions.question_en: The off-tracking produced during a left turn becomes larger as the wheelbase becomes shorter.
questions.question_ja: 左折するときに生じる内輪差は、ホイールベースが短いほど、大きくなり危険である。
questions.explanation: False. Off-tracking generally becomes greater as the wheelbase becomes longer, not shorter.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that there is an uphill or downhill slope ahead.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先に上り坂や下り坂があることを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured warning sign indicates a tunnel ahead.

questions.question_en: If you hold an ordinary driver’s license, you may drive a moped, and after accumulating a certain amount of driving experience you may also drive an ordinary motorcycle.
questions.question_ja: 普通免許を持っていれば原動機付自転車を運転できるが、一定期間の運転経験をつむと、普通自動二輪車も運転することができる。
questions.explanation: False. Driving experience with an ordinary license does not automatically grant motorcycle-driving privileges; the appropriate motorcycle license is required.

questions.question_en: You must not provide or recommend alcohol to a person who is about to drive.
questions.question_ja: これから車を運転しようとする人に、酒を出したり、勧めたりしてはいけない。
questions.explanation: True. Supplying or encouraging alcohol for a person who will drive contributes to drunk driving and is prohibited.

questions.question_en: You may sound the horn at a place with a “Sound Horn” sign or when unavoidable in order to prevent danger.
questions.question_ja: 「警笛鳴らせ」の標識がある場所や、危険をさけるためやむを得ないときは、警音器を鳴らすことができる。
questions.explanation: True. Those are recognized situations in which horn use is required or permitted.

questions.question_en: When you are in a hurry, that is an unavoidable circumstance, so on a road without traffic lanes you may drive near the center.
questions.question_ja: 急いでいるときは、やむを得ない場合であるから、車両通行帯のない道路では中央寄りを走ってもよい。
questions.explanation: False. Being in a hurry does not justify abandoning the normal left-side road position.

questions.question_en: When overtaking by entering the right side of the road, even an oncoming vehicle that appears far away may be approaching faster than expected, so it is better to wait for it to pass and then overtake with ample safety margin.
questions.question_ja: 道路の右側部分にはみ出して追越しをするときは、反対方向から進行してくる車が遠くに見える場合であっても、意外と間近にせまっていることがあるので、その通過を待った後に、余裕を持って追越す方がよい。
questions.explanation: True. Distance and closing speed can be misjudged, so waiting removes the conflict with oncoming traffic.

questions.question_en: A motor vehicle facing this signal may enter and pass through the intersection after first stopping and checking other traffic.
questions.question_ja: この信号に対面する自動車は、ほかの交通に注意しながら一時停止すれば交差点に進入し、通過することができる。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured steady yellow signal means stop if you can do so safely before the stopping position; it is not a stop-and-proceed signal.

questions.question_en: At a place with this sign, only ordinary passenger cars may travel within the streetcar track area.
questions.question_ja: この標識があるところでは、普通自動車だけが軌道敷内を通行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. The pictured sign permits the applicable motor vehicles to use the streetcar track area; the permission is not limited only to ordinary cars.

questions.question_en: At a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing and within 30 meters before it, both overtaking and passing another vehicle to move ahead of it are prohibited.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道や自転車横断帯とその手前から30メートル以内の場所は、追越しも追抜きも禁止されている。
questions.explanation: True. The protected zone prohibits not only formal overtaking but also passing alongside a vehicle and getting ahead of it.

questions.question_en: When you see a pedestrian or bicycle ahead, because they may behave unexpectedly you should prepare to avoid them with the steering wheel at any moment.
questions.question_ja: 前方に歩行者や自転車を認めたときは、予期しない行動をするかもしれないので、いつでもハンドルで避けられるように身構えて運転する。
questions.explanation: False. The primary safe response is to reduce speed, increase distance, and be ready to brake; relying on sudden steering can create a collision with other traffic.

questions.question_en: After overtaking, when returning to the original lane, it is good to continue until the overtaken vehicle is visible in the rear-view mirror, signal left, and return gradually to the left lane.
questions.question_ja: 追越しをした後、もとの車線に戻るときは、ルームミラーに車が見える程度まで進んでから、左の方向指示器を出し、ゆるやかに左の車線に戻るのがよい。
questions.explanation: True. This provides adequate clearance before moving back in front of the overtaken vehicle.

questions.question_en: When parking an automatic car, keep the brake pedal depressed, apply the parking brake securely, move the selector to P, and then turn off the engine.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車を駐車するときは、ブレーキペダルを踏んだままハンドブレーキを確実にかけ、チェンジレバーを「P」の位置に入れてからエンジンを切るのがよい。
questions.explanation: True. This sequence secures the vehicle before engine shutdown and prevents unintended movement.

questions.question_en: If you absolutely must use a mobile phone while driving, use a hands-free device so that your eyes do not leave the road and you do not need to hold the phone while talking.
questions.question_ja: 運転中に、どうしても携帯電話を使用する必要があるときは、操作の際に視線が前方からはずれることなく、また、手に持って通話する必要がなくなるハンズフリー装置を使用する。
questions.explanation: The source marks this True because the hands-free device is intended to avoid holding or looking at the phone. However, current National Police Agency guidance says that if you need to use a smartphone or mobile phone, stop in a safe place before using it.

questions.question_en: There was clearly nobody at the crosswalk or bicycle crossing ahead, so I overtook the vehicle in front 30 meters before it.
questions.question_ja: 前方の横断歩道や自転車横断帯に明らかに人がいなかったので、30メートル手前で前の車を追越した。
questions.explanation: False. Overtaking or passing another vehicle is prohibited at a crosswalk or bicycle crossing and within 30 meters before it, even when nobody is visibly crossing.

questions.question_en: At an uncontrolled intersection of roads of about the same width, excluding a roundabout, a streetcar was already in the intersection. Because traffic from the left has priority, I may continue as I am.
questions.question_ja: 交通整理の行われていない、道幅の同じような道路の交差点（環状交差点を除く）に車で入ろうとしたとき、すでに交差点に入っている路面電車があっても、左方優先であるから自分の車はそのまま進行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. A vehicle must not proceed on the basis of left-side priority when doing so would obstruct a streetcar that is already in the intersection.

questions.question_en: When I became sleepy while driving, I opened the window for fresh air and listened to the radio to refresh myself while continuing to drive.
questions.question_ja: 運転中、眠たくなったときは、眠気をさますため、窓を開けて新鮮な空気を入れたり、ラジオを聞くなど気分転換を図りながら運転する。
questions.explanation: False. These measures do not make it safe to continue driving when sleepy. The safe response is to stop in a safe place and rest.

questions.question_en: Two friends drank alcohol. When leaving, one asked the less-drunk friend to drive. Because the person who asked was not driving, that person can receive an administrative penalty but not a criminal penalty.
questions.question_ja: 友人と二人で酒を飲み、帰る際あまり酔っていない友人に運転を依頼したが、依頼した者は運転していないので、行政処分の対象とはなるが、刑事処分の対象とはならない。
questions.explanation: False. Asking or assisting a person to drive after drinking can also result in criminal responsibility; liability is not limited to the person actually driving.

questions.question_en: The distance traveled from when the driver senses danger until the brakes begin to work, plus the distance from when the brakes begin to work until the vehicle stops, is called the stopping distance.
questions.question_ja: 運転者が、危険を感じてからブレーキを踏んでブレーキがきき始めるまでと、ブレーキがきき始めてから車が停止するまでの距離を停止距離という。
questions.explanation: True. Stopping distance is the total of the reaction distance and the braking distance.

questions.question_en: When reversing an automatic vehicle, check behind, shift the selector to D, release the parking brake, gradually release the brake pedal, and gently press the accelerator.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車で後退するときは、後方の安全を目で確認しながら、チェンジレバーをDに入れ、ハンドブレーキを戻し、ブレーキペダルを徐々に放し、アクセルペダルを静かに踏んで発進する。
questions.explanation: False. D is the forward-driving position. To reverse, the selector must be placed in R after confirming safety.

questions.question_en: When children are playing on the road, you may sound the horn as a warning and pass without slowing down.
questions.question_ja: こどもが道路で遊んでいるのを見かけたときは、警音器を鳴らして警告すれば、徐行しないで通行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. Sounding the horn does not remove the duty to drive cautiously. When children may enter the vehicle's path, the driver must slow down as necessary and be ready to stop.

questions.question_en: On a road with two traffic lanes in the same direction, faster vehicles must use the right lane and slower vehicles must use the left lane.
questions.question_ja: 同一方向に二つの車両通行帯がある道路では、速度の速い車が右側、遅い車が左側の車両通行帯を通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. With two lanes in the same direction, vehicles normally use the left lane; the right lane is not simply assigned to faster vehicles.

questions.question_en: When turning right at a congested intersection, it is acceptable to cut through a gap in oncoming traffic and make the shortest possible right turn.
questions.question_ja: 混雑している交差点を右折する場合は、対向車の切れ目をぬって最短距離で右折してもかまわない。
questions.explanation: False. A right turn must be made safely and according to the prescribed position and path; congestion does not permit cutting across the intersection unsafely.

questions.question_en: When turning right or left at an intersection, excluding a roundabout, the signal should be started when the vehicle reaches a point 30 meters before the place where the turn will be made.
questions.question_ja: 交差点（環状交差点を除く）で右折または左折をする場合の合図を行う場所は、その行為をしようとする地点から30メートル手前の地点に達したときである。
questions.explanation: True. For a right or left turn, the turn signal is given from about 30 meters before the turning point and continued until the turn is completed.

questions.question_en: A motorized bicycle may use a bicycle path only when no bicycles are using it.
questions.question_ja: 自転車道は、自転車が通行していないときに限り、原動機付自転車も通行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. A bicycle path is for vehicles legally permitted to use it; an ordinary motorized bicycle does not become permitted merely because no bicycle is present.

questions.question_en: When a vehicle turns left, off-tracking occurs because the rear wheels pass inside the path of the front wheels, but this does not occur when turning right.
questions.question_ja: 車が交差点を左折するときは内輪差（曲がるとき後輪が前輪より内側をとおること）が生じるが、右折するときは生じない。
questions.explanation: False. Off-tracking occurs when a vehicle turns in either direction; the rear wheels follow a path inside the front wheels.

questions.question_en: On an ordinary road with no sign or marking specifying another limit, the maximum speed for an ordinary cargo vehicle is 60 km/h.
questions.question_ja: 標識や標示で指定されていない一般道路における普通貨物自動車の最高速度は、時速60キロメートルである。
questions.explanation: True. The statutory maximum speed on an ordinary road is 60 km/h unless a different maximum speed is specified.

questions.question_en: During heavy holiday traffic, motorcycles may use the roadside strip because traffic is congested.
questions.question_ja: 帰省ラッシュで交通が混雑しているときに限って、二輪車は路側帯を通ってもよい。
questions.explanation: False. Traffic congestion does not make the roadside strip a normal traffic lane for motorcycles.

questions.question_en: The basic way to approach a bicycle crossing is the same as when approaching a pedestrian crossing.
questions.question_ja: 自転車横断帯に近づくときの考え方は、基本的に横断歩道に近づく場合と同じと考えてよい。
questions.explanation: True. Drivers approaching a bicycle crossing must check for bicycles that are crossing or about to cross and must give them priority in the same basic manner required at a crosswalk.

questions.question_en: Even where U-turns are prohibited, a U-turn may be made when traffic is congested because of an accident.
questions.question_ja: 転回が禁止されている場所であっても、交通事故などで混雑している場合は転回してもよい。
questions.explanation: False. Congestion or an accident does not cancel a U-turn prohibition.

questions.question_en: The police officer's hand signal shown has the same meaning as a green traffic light for traffic moving in the direction of the arrow.
questions.question_ja: この図のような警察官の手信号は、矢印の方向の交通に対しては、青色の灯火の信号と同じ意味である。
questions.explanation: True. For the traffic direction shown in the diagram, the officer's hand signal permits traffic to proceed, equivalent to a green signal.

questions.question_en: When overtaking, first move toward the right while turning on the right indicator, and then check that it is safe behind.
questions.question_ja: 追越しをするときは、まず右に寄りながら右側の方向指示器を出し、次に後方の安全を確かめるのがよい。
questions.explanation: False. Safety must be checked before changing position. The driver should check mirrors and the rear/side area, signal, and then change course only when safe.

questions.question_en: The vehicle ahead was repeatedly lighting its brake lamps and traveling at an uneven speed, so I sounded the horn to make it give way for safety.
questions.question_ja: 前車がブレーキ灯をときどき点灯させながら一定しない速度で走行していたので、危険防止のため警音器を鳴らして進路をゆずらせた。
questions.explanation: False. The horn may be used only where required or when necessary to prevent danger; it must not be used simply to force another vehicle to give way.

questions.question_en: A cargo vehicle with a maximum payload of 2,500 kilograms may be driven with an ordinary driver's license.
questions.question_ja: 最大積載量が2,500キログラムの貨物自動車は、普通免許で運転することができる。
questions.explanation: False. A current ordinary license does not cover a vehicle with a maximum payload of 2,500 kg; that payload exceeds the ordinary-license vehicle limit.

questions.question_en: When starting from a stop at the left edge of the road, signal in the same way as when changing course to the right while traveling in the same direction.
questions.question_ja: 道路の左側端に停車していて発進するときは、同一方向に進行しながら進路を右方に変えるときと同じ要領で合図をする。
questions.explanation: True. Pulling out from the left edge involves moving right into the traffic stream, so the right-turn indicator is used while checking surrounding traffic.

questions.question_en: Overtaking is prohibited even inside a tunnel that has traffic lanes.
questions.question_ja: 車両通行帯のあるトンネルでも、追越すことはできない。
questions.explanation: False. The general tunnel overtaking prohibition applies to a tunnel without traffic lanes. A tunnel with marked traffic lanes is not automatically covered by that prohibition.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that there is a merging-traffic point ahead.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先に合流交通の地点があることを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The warning sign shown indicates merging traffic ahead.

questions.question_en: When reversing a vehicle, pedestrians or other vehicles may have come close behind, so the driver must carefully check the rear.
questions.question_ja: 自動車を後退させるときは、歩行者やほかの自動車が近くにきていることがあるので、後方の確認を十分に行う必要がある。
questions.explanation: True. Reversing creates a large blind area, so the driver must confirm that the rear and surrounding area are safe before and while moving backward.

questions.question_en: When there is an obstruction ahead in your lane, stop before the obstruction and give way to oncoming traffic.
questions.question_ja: 進路の前方に障害物があるときは、その手前で停止して対向車に道をゆずる。
questions.explanation: True. The vehicle whose side is obstructed should yield because moving around the obstruction requires entering the opposing side of the road.

questions.question_en: At a tram stop without a safety island, a tram is stopped and passengers are getting on or off. If there is at least 1.5 meters of space between your vehicle and the tram, you may pass without concern.
questions.question_ja: 安全地帯のない停留所で路面電車が止まっていて乗り降りする人がいる場合、電車との間に1.5メートル以上の間隔があれば気にせず通過してよい。
questions.explanation: False. When passengers are boarding or leaving a stopped tram at a stop without a safety island, the driver must stop and wait; a 1.5-meter gap does not by itself permit passing.

questions.question_en: Starting uphill is difficult, so a vehicle going downhill should give way to a vehicle going uphill. However, if a passing place is nearby, even the uphill vehicle should enter it and wait when appropriate.
questions.question_ja: 上り坂では発進が難しいので、下りの車が上りの車に道をゆずるが、近くに待避所があるときは、上りの車でもその待避所に入って待つとよい。
questions.explanation: True. Uphill vehicles are generally given priority on a narrow slope because restarting uphill is difficult, but a nearby passing place may make it safer and easier for the uphill vehicle to wait there.

questions.question_en: If the vehicle ahead signals to change course in order to enter a traffic lane designated by a sign or marking, you must not obstruct that course change unless avoiding it would require sudden braking or sudden steering.
questions.question_ja: 前の車が、標識などにより指定された車両通行帯を通行するために進路を変えようと合図をした場合は、急ブレーキや急ハンドルでさけなければならないようなとき以外は、その進路変更を妨げてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A driver must not interfere with a lawful course change of this kind when the change can be accommodated safely.

questions.question_en: My lane was congested, so I considered it unavoidable and drove in a bus-only lane.
questions.question_ja: 通行しているレーンの交通量が多く混雑していたので、やむを得ない場合であると思いバス専用レーンを通行した。
questions.explanation: False. Ordinary congestion is not a reason for an unauthorized vehicle to use a bus-only lane.

questions.question_en: When stopping a vehicle, except when unavoidable, the driver should apply the brakes in several stages so that following vehicles are warned that the vehicle is slowing and stopping.
questions.question_ja: 車を停止させようとするときは、やむを得ない場合を除き、ブレーキを数回に分けて踏み、後車に停止することを知らせるという配慮が必要である。
questions.explanation: True. Progressive braking helps communicate deceleration to following traffic and reduces the risk of a rear-end collision.

questions.question_en: You must not overtake another vehicle near a road bend or on a steep downhill slope.
questions.question_ja: 道路の曲がり角付近やこう配の急な下り坂では、ほかの自動車を追越してはいけない。
questions.explanation: True. Road bends and steep downhill slopes are among the places where overtaking is prohibited.

questions.question_en: The signal ahead turned yellow. I was near the stopping position and could not stop safely, so I entered the intersection, stopped inside it, and waited for the signal to change.
questions.question_ja: 前方の信号が黄色に変わったとき、交差点の手前の停止位置に近づいていたが、安全に停止することができなかったので、交差点に進入して停止し、信号が変わるのを待った。
questions.explanation: False. If a vehicle cannot stop safely when the light turns yellow, it may continue through; it must not enter merely to stop inside the intersection.

questions.question_en: Unlike four-wheeled vehicles, motorcycles can turn in a small space, so when passing pedestrians they do not need to slow down or keep a safe distance.
questions.question_ja: 二輪車は四輪車と違い小回りがきくので、歩行者のそばを通るときでも徐行したり安全な間隔をとる必要はない。
questions.explanation: False. Motorcycles must also keep a safe side clearance from pedestrians or slow down when sufficient clearance cannot be maintained.

questions.question_en: This sign means that vehicles carrying more than 5.5 tons of cargo may not pass.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、積み荷の重さが5.5トンをこえる車の通行ができないことを意味している。
questions.explanation: False. The sign limits vehicles by gross vehicle weight, not by the weight of the cargo alone.

questions.question_en: When you see an ordinary passenger car displaying a beginner-driver mark, except when unavoidable to avoid danger, you must not crowd it from the side or forcefully cut in directly in front of it.
questions.question_ja: 初心者マークをつけた普通乗用車を認めたときは、危険を避けるためやむを得ない場合を除いては、その車の側方に幅寄せしたり、前方へ無理に割り込んではならない。
questions.explanation: True. Other drivers must not unnecessarily crowd or cut in front of a vehicle displaying the beginner-driver mark.

questions.question_en: Where the left-hand part of the road is not wide enough for passage, a vehicle may travel partly into the right-hand part of the road.
questions.question_ja: 道路の左側部分の幅が通行するのに十分でないところでは、右側部分にはみ出して通行することができる。
questions.explanation: True. When the left side is insufficient for passage, crossing into the right side may be permitted when necessary and safe, subject to the applicable restrictions.

questions.question_en: At a place with this sign, vehicles are prohibited not only from crossing the road but also from making U-turns and reversing.
questions.question_ja: この標識のある場所では、車は横断だけではなく、転回や後退も禁止されている。
questions.explanation: False. The sign shown is 'No vehicle crossing.' It prohibits crossing the road to enter or leave roadside premises as specified; it does not itself prohibit every U-turn or reverse movement.

questions.question_en: An elderly driver is a person aged 80 or older and must display the elderly-driver mark at the specified positions on the front and rear of an ordinary vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 高齢運転者とは、80歳以上であり、普通自動車の前と後ろの定められた位置に高齢者マークをつけなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The elderly-driver mark concerns drivers aged 70 or older whose age-related physical changes may affect driving, and displaying it is not a blanket mandatory requirement for everyone aged 80 or older.

questions.question_en: When the signal in your direction is flashing yellow, it is intended for pedestrians, so vehicles may proceed without paying attention to other traffic.
questions.question_ja: 進行方向の信号が黄色の灯火の点滅をしている場合は、歩行者向けであるから、車はほかの交通に注意することなく通行することができる。
questions.explanation: False. A flashing yellow signal allows a vehicle to proceed only with caution; the driver must pay attention to other traffic.

questions.question_en: A pedestrian was about to cross at a crosswalk, so I stopped. Because I was in a hurry, I sounded the horn as a warning and passed before the pedestrian.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道を横断しようとしている歩行者がいたので一時停止したが、急いでいたので警音器を鳴らして注意をうながし、歩行者より先に通過した。
questions.explanation: False. A pedestrian crossing or about to cross at a crosswalk has priority. The driver must stop and must not use the horn to pressure the pedestrian into yielding.

questions.question_en: Some supplementary signs specify a type of vehicle and may use prescribed abbreviations, so drivers should know the abbreviations used for vehicle types.
questions.question_ja: 補助標識の中には、車両の種類を特定するものがあり、その場合、定められた略称を用いることがあるので、車両の種類の略称を知っておくようにする。
questions.explanation: True. Supplementary signs can limit a regulation to particular vehicle classes, and prescribed abbreviated vehicle names may be used.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that the road ahead curves to the right.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先の道路が右カーブになっていることを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The warning sign shown indicates a right-hand curve ahead.

questions.question_en: This road marking indicates the end of a 'No U-turn' section.
questions.question_ja: この標示は、その場所が「転回禁止」の終わりであることを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The yellow road marking shown indicates that U-turning is prohibited; it does not indicate the end of the restriction.

questions.question_en: A learner-driver practice sign must be attached at the prescribed positions on both the front and rear of the vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 仮免許練習標識は、車の前と後ろの定められた位置につけなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A vehicle used for practice under a learner's permit must display the prescribed learner-practice signs at the required front and rear positions.

questions.question_en: At a place with this sign, pedestrians must not cross the road.
questions.question_ja: この標識がある場所では、歩行者は道路を横断してはならない。
questions.explanation: True. The sign shown means 'No pedestrian crossing.' Pedestrians must not cross the section of road where the prohibition applies.

questions.question_en: When this signboard is displayed, a vehicle may turn left even if the traffic signal ahead is red or yellow, but it must not obstruct pedestrians or bicycles crossing in accordance with their signal.
questions.question_ja: この標示板があるときは、前方の信号が赤や黄であっても左折できるが、信号に従って横断している歩行者や自転車の通行を妨げてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. The sign shown is the left-turn-permitted sign. A vehicle may turn left despite a red or yellow signal, but crossing pedestrians and bicycles retain priority.

questions.question_en: I was about to change course, but a vehicle was approaching from behind, so I stopped the course change and let that vehicle pass.
questions.question_ja: 進路変更をしようとしたところ、後方に車が接近していたので、進路変更をやめて進路をゆずった。
questions.explanation: True. A course change must not be made when it would interfere with a vehicle approaching from behind; waiting and yielding is the safe action.

questions.question_en: During the time shown by this marking, vehicles other than buses cannot use this lane.
questions.question_ja: この標示に示されているレーンの時間帯は、バス以外の自動車は通行できない。
questions.explanation: False. The marking shown is a bus-priority lane, not a bus-exclusive lane. Other permitted vehicles may use it but must not obstruct a route bus and must leave the lane as required when a bus approaches.

questions.question_en: When an automatic vehicle's selector is in a position other than P or N, the vehicle may move by creep even without pressing the accelerator, so the brake pedal must be held firmly while stopped.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車のチェンジレバーが「P」や「N」以外の位置にあるときは、アクセルペダルを踏まなくてもクリープ現象で車が動き出すことがあるので、停止中はブレーキペダルをしっかり踏んでおかなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Automatic vehicles can creep when a driving range is selected, so keeping the brake pedal firmly depressed prevents unintended movement.

questions.question_en: Because an automatic vehicle has little engine-braking effect, when driving downhill it is best to control speed using the foot brake and the parking brake.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車は、エンジンブレーキの効果が小さいので、下り坂では、フットブレーキとハンドブレーキで速度を調節しながら走行するのがよい。
questions.explanation: False. The parking brake is not used as a normal speed-control brake while driving downhill. Use an appropriate lower gear or range to obtain engine braking and use the foot brake as necessary.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that you must not drive at a speed below 30 km/h.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、時速30キロメートルに達しない速度で走ってはならないことを示している。
questions.explanation: True. The sign shown is a minimum-speed sign. It requires vehicles subject to the sign to travel at 30 km/h or more unless slowing is necessary for safety or another rule requires it.

questions.question_en: I had been working through the night and was short of sleep, so I canceled my trip by car.
questions.question_ja: 徹夜の仕事が続き、睡眠不足であったので、車での外出を中止した。
questions.explanation: True. Sleep deprivation reduces attention and reaction ability. If you are not in a condition to drive safely, you should not drive.

questions.question_en: When overtaking, after turning on the right indicator and waiting about three seconds, you may accelerate above the maximum speed limit.
questions.question_ja: 追越しをするときは、右の方向指示器を出して約3秒後に、最高速度の制限をこえて加速してよい。
questions.explanation: False. Signaling does not permit exceeding the legal maximum speed. The speed limit still applies while overtaking.

questions.question_en: When changing course, you must take sufficient care so that you do not cause trouble or danger to other vehicles.
questions.question_ja: 進路を変更しようとするときは、ほかの自動車などに迷惑をかけないように十分な気配りが必要である。
questions.explanation: True. A course change must be made only after checking that it can be done safely without obstructing surrounding traffic.

questions.question_en: When driving an automatic vehicle, pressing the accelerator strongly can automatically shift the transmission down one gear and produce rapid acceleration.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車で走行するときは、アクセルペダルを強く踏み込むと、自動的にギアが一段下へ低くなり、急加速することができる。
questions.explanation: True. This is the kick-down function: strong accelerator input can cause an automatic transmission to select a lower gear for stronger acceleration.

questions.question_en: When driving, it is not dangerous to sit with your body at an angle as long as that position feels easy to drive in.
questions.question_ja: 運転するときは、体を斜めにしても、運転がしやすければ危険ではない。
questions.explanation: False. The driver should use a proper driving posture so that the steering wheel, pedals, mirrors, and controls can be operated accurately and quickly.

questions.question_en: With a roadside strip marked by a white solid line and a white broken line like this, a vehicle may not enter the strip to park or stop.
questions.question_ja: このような白の実線と破線の標示がある路側帯は、車はその中に入って駐車や停車することはできない。
questions.explanation: True. Where this solid-and-broken white roadside-strip marking is used, vehicles must not enter the roadside strip for parking or stopping.

questions.question_en: A person who has an ordinary learner's permit may ride a motorized bicycle if it is for practice.
questions.question_ja: 普通仮免許を受けた者は、練習のためであれば、原動機付自転車を運転してよい。
questions.explanation: False. An ordinary learner's permit authorizes practice in the class of vehicle covered by that learner permit under the required supervision and conditions; it does not itself authorize riding a motorized bicycle.

questions.question_en: When reversing an automatic vehicle, firmly press the brake pedal, visually confirm safety, shift the selector to R, release the parking brake, gradually release the brake pedal, and then gently press the accelerator.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車で後退するときは、しっかりとブレーキペダルを踏んで、目で確かめながらチェンジレバーを「R」に入れ、ハンドブレーキを戻してブレーキペダルを徐々に放してから、アクセルペダルを静かに踏むのがよい。
questions.explanation: True. R is the reverse position. The sequence keeps the vehicle controlled while the driver confirms the rear and surrounding area before moving.

questions.question_en: This sign is a guide sign used on expressways.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、高速道路で用いられる案内標識である
questions.explanation: True. The sign shown is an expressway guide sign used to provide route or destination guidance on expressways.

questions.question_en: This sign warns that the road shoulder ahead is likely to collapse.
questions.question_ja: この標識のあるところは、この先の道路の路肩が崩れやすいので注意する。
questions.explanation: False. The warning sign shown indicates falling rocks, not a weak or collapsing road shoulder.

questions.question_en: When passing beside a stopped vehicle, a driver must be careful because a person may suddenly come out from behind the vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 車の運転者は、止まっている車のそばを通るときは、車のかげから人が飛び出すことがあるので注意して通過しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A stopped vehicle can hide pedestrians or cyclists, so the driver must reduce risk by checking carefully and being ready for someone to emerge.

questions.question_en: At an uncontrolled intersection with poor visibility, if there are no other vehicles, you may pass without slowing down.
questions.question_ja: 交通整理の行われていない見通しの悪い交差点であっても、ほかの車がなければ徐行しないで通過することができる。
questions.explanation: False. At an uncontrolled intersection with poor visibility, the driver must slow down as required even when another vehicle is not immediately visible.

questions.question_en: Motorized bicycles are not allowed to use a lane reserved exclusively for route buses.
questions.question_ja: 路線バスの専用通行帯は、原動機付自転車の通行はできない。
questions.explanation: False. Ordinary motorized bicycles are among the vehicle types that may use a route-bus-only lane under the applicable rule; the restriction is not an absolute ban on them.

questions.question_en: When crossing a sidewalk or roadside strip to enter or leave a gasoline station or other roadside property, you must stop once before crossing, whether or not a pedestrian is present.
questions.question_ja: 道路に面したガソリンスタンドなどに出入りするために歩道や路側帯を横切る場合は、歩行者がいてもいなくても、一時停止しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Before crossing a sidewalk or roadside strip to enter or leave roadside premises, a vehicle must stop immediately before it and must not obstruct pedestrians.

questions.question_en: Because this is a 'No travel except in the designated direction' sign, vehicles at this intersection cannot go straight or turn right.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、指定方向外進行禁止の標識なので、この交差点では直進や右折することができない。
questions.explanation: False. The sign shown is a lane-direction sign indicating the permitted direction for the lane where it is installed; it is not the circular 'No travel except in designated directions' regulatory sign described in the statement.

questions.question_en: When approaching a crosswalk, even when it is clear that nobody is crossing or about to cross, you must still travel at a speed that allows you to stop before it.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道に近づいたときは、横断する人や横断しようとしている人がいないことが明らかな場合でも、その手前で停止できるような速度で進まなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The duty to approach at a speed that permits stopping applies unless it is clear that no pedestrian or bicycle is crossing or about to cross.

questions.question_en: A line of elementary-school children was ahead, so I passed beside them at a slow speed.
questions.question_ja: 前方で小学生が列になっていたので、その横を徐行して通過した。
questions.explanation: True. When passing children or other people who may enter the roadway unexpectedly, slowing down and passing with special care is appropriate.

questions.question_en: While riding a motorcycle, I noticed a vehicle behind trying to overtake me. Using the motorcycle's maneuverability, I increased speed and overtook the vehicle ahead.
questions.question_ja: 二輪車で進行中、後方の車が自分の車を追越そうとしているのに気づいたが、二輪車の機動性を生かして、速度を上げ、前の車を追越した。
questions.explanation: False. A driver must not increase speed to interfere with a vehicle that is overtaking. The motorcycle should maintain safe control and allow the overtaking vehicle to pass.

questions.question_en: When passing beside a safety island, you must always slow down whether or not a pedestrian is on the safety island.
questions.question_ja: 安全地帯のそばを通るときは、安全地帯に歩行者がいるいないに関係なく徐行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The special slow-driving requirement applies when pedestrians are on the safety island; it is not an unconditional requirement merely because the island exists.

questions.question_en: Except in specially permitted cases, vehicles must travel on the left-hand part of the road from the center of the roadway, or from the center line when one is marked.
questions.question_ja: 車は、特に決められた場合のほかは、道路の中央（中央線があるときは、その中央線）から左の部分を通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Japan uses left-side traffic, so vehicles normally travel on the left side of the road's center or center line unless an exception applies.

questions.question_en: Because an automatic vehicle can be driven safely with one hand, it is acceptable to hold a mobile phone and talk while driving.
questions.question_ja: オートマチック車を運転するときは、片手で運転しても十分安全に運転できるので、携帯電話を手に持って話しをしながら運転してよい。
questions.explanation: False. Holding and using a mobile phone while driving is prohibited and dangerously reduces the driver's ability to observe and control the vehicle.

questions.question_en: The elderly-driver mark must be attached at a position determined according to the driver's physical ability when driving an ordinary vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 高齢者マークは、普通自動車を運転するときに、身体の機能に応じて定められた位置につけなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The elderly-driver mark is displayed at prescribed positions on the front and rear; it is not positioned according to the driver's individual physical condition, and its display is not a blanket mandatory requirement in the way stated.

questions.question_en: With the police officer's hand signal shown, traffic moving in the direction of the arrows must stop before the stop line.
questions.question_ja: このような警察官の手信号は、矢印の方向の交通は停止線の前で停止しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. For the directions shown, the officer's raised-arm signal requires traffic to stop at the stopping position.

questions.question_en: On a rainy day, when passing an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, you should move as far left as possible and drive on the road shoulder.
questions.question_ja: 雨の日、狭い道路で対向車と行き違うときは、できるだけ左側に寄り、路肩を通行したほうがよい。
questions.explanation: False. The road shoulder may be unsafe or unsuitable for vehicle travel, especially in rain. Move left only within a safe, lawful part of the roadway and do not deliberately drive onto the shoulder merely to pass.

questions.question_en: A microbus with a seating capacity of 11 people may be driven with an ordinary driver's license.
questions.question_ja: 乗車定員11人のマイクロバスは、普通免許で運転できる。
questions.explanation: False. A vehicle with a seating capacity of 11 is outside the passenger-capacity limit for an ordinary license and requires the appropriate higher class of license.

questions.question_en: When turning left at an intersection, the rear wheels pass inside the path of the front wheels, so the driver must be careful to avoid trapping or striking someone on the left side.
questions.question_ja: 車で交差点を左折するときは、後輪が前輪より内側を通るので、巻き込み事故を起こさないよう注意する。
questions.explanation: True. This inward tracking of the rear wheels creates a left-side blind and sweep area, so special attention is needed for bicycles, motorcycles, and pedestrians.

questions.question_en: At a railroad crossing controlled by a traffic signal, you may proceed according to the signal, so you do not need to stop once before the crossing.
questions.question_ja: 信号機のある踏切では、信号に従って通行することができるので、一時停止する必要はない。
questions.explanation: True. Where a railroad crossing is controlled by a traffic signal, a vehicle may proceed according to that signal without the usual mandatory stop, while still confirming that passage is safe.

questions.question_en: A motorized bicycle facing this signal may proceed in the direction of the arrow at every intersection.
questions.question_ja: この信号に対面する原動機付自転車は、すべての交差点で矢印の方向に進むことができる。
questions.explanation: False. A motorized bicycle may not follow the right-turn arrow in every situation. Where the two-stage right-turn rule applies, it must turn right using the prescribed two-stage method rather than following the arrow as a direct right turn.

questions.question_en: At a staggered or time-difference traffic signal, even if oncoming traffic starts moving, your signal may not be green, so you must check the signal facing you.
questions.question_ja: 時差式信号のときは、対向車が発進しても前方の信号が青であるとは限らないので、必ず前方の信号を確認する必要がある。
questions.explanation: True. Oncoming traffic can receive a different signal phase. A driver must obey the signal facing their own direction rather than infer it from another traffic stream.

questions.question_en: Overtaking means changing course to move ahead of a vehicle traveling in front. Because it involves complex driving operations, overtaking should be avoided when possible and the vehicle should be driven at a safe speed.
questions.question_ja: 追越しとは、車が進路を変えて進行中の前の車の前方に出ることであり、複雑な運転操作を伴うので、追越しはできるだけ避け、安全な速度で走るのがよい。
questions.explanation: True. Overtaking requires several checks and course changes and creates additional risk, so it should be done only when necessary and clearly safe.

questions.question_en: A vehicle displaying the elderly-driver mark has priority at intersections and similar places.
questions.question_ja: 高齢者マークをつけている車は、交差点などで優先通行権がある。
questions.explanation: False. The elderly-driver mark asks other drivers to show consideration; it does not give the marked vehicle a general right of priority.

questions.question_en: If you splash mud or water onto a pedestrian, the driver is responsible even if the vehicle was traveling slowly.
questions.question_ja: 歩行者に泥や水をはねてしまったときは、たとえ徐行しても運転者の責任である。
questions.explanation: True. Drivers must take measures such as slowing to avoid splashing mud or water on others; simply driving slowly does not remove responsibility if splashing occurs.

questions.question_en: For an ordinary passenger car traveling at 40 km/h on a dry asphalt road, the stopping distance is about 22 meters.
questions.question_ja: 時速40キロメートルで走行している普通乗用車の停止距離は、乾燥したアスファルト道路の場合で、約22メートル程度となる。
questions.explanation: True. The standard teaching value for a passenger car at 40 km/h on dry asphalt is approximately 22 meters from recognition of danger to a complete stop.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that there is a crosswalk ahead for schoolchildren or kindergarten children.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先に学童、園児のための横断歩道があることを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The sign shown means a pedestrian-only road or pedestrian-only passage. It is not a warning sign for a schoolchild or kindergarten crosswalk ahead.

questions.question_en: Children may become absorbed in something that interests them and suddenly run into the road, so drivers must be especially careful when children are nearby.
questions.question_ja: こどもは、興味のあるものに夢中になり突然路上に飛び出したりするので、こどもがいる場合は、運転者は特に注意しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. Children can move unpredictably and may not judge traffic accurately, so drivers must anticipate sudden movement and be ready to slow or stop.

questions.question_en: A pedestrian was crossing at an intersection without a crosswalk, so I stopped so as not to obstruct the pedestrian and waited until the crossing was completed.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道のない交差点で歩行者が横断していたので、その通行を妨げないように一時停止をし、歩行者が横断し終わるのを待った。
questions.explanation: True. At an intersection or immediately near it where there is no crosswalk, a driver must not obstruct a pedestrian who is crossing.

questions.question_en: At a place with this sign, vehicles may park from 8:00 to 20:00.
questions.question_ja: この標識があるところでは、車は8時から20時まで駐車することができる。
questions.explanation: False. The sign shown prohibits parking during the indicated time, 8:00 to 20:00; it does not permit parking during those hours.

questions.question_en: Inside a tunnel, the visible area feels restricted and it is difficult to judge conditions ahead and behind accurately, increasing the risk of driving error. Therefore, overtaking is prohibited in a tunnel without traffic lanes.
questions.question_ja: トンネル内では、運転者の見える範囲は狭く感じられ、また前方や後方の状況を正確に認知しにくく、運転を誤る危険性が高いので、車両通行帯のないトンネルでは追越しをしてはならない。
questions.explanation: True. A tunnel without marked traffic lanes is one of the places where overtaking is prohibited.

questions.question_en: On a narrow road, the vehicle ahead suddenly reversed toward me, so I sounded the horn to avoid danger.
questions.question_ja: 狭い道で、前の車が急に後退してきたので、警音器を鳴らして危険を避けた。
questions.explanation: True. The horn may be used when necessary to prevent an immediate danger, as in this situation.

questions.question_en: The left-hand portion of the road was 7 meters wide. Because there was no oncoming vehicle, I crossed the center into the right-hand portion to overtake.
questions.question_ja: 道路の左側部分の幅が７メートルのところで、対向車がなかったので、追越しのため中央から右側部分にはみ出して通行した。
questions.explanation: False. When the left-hand part of the road is at least 6 meters wide, a vehicle may not cross into the right-hand part simply for overtaking.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates that there is a Y-shaped intersection ahead.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、この先にY形の交差点があることを示している。
questions.explanation: False. The sign shown is a regulatory sign specifying the permitted directions of travel; it is not a warning sign for a Y-shaped intersection.

questions.question_en: When changing course, signaling early inconveniences other vehicles, so the safest method is to turn the steering wheel immediately after giving the signal.
questions.question_ja: 進路変更するときは、合図を早めにするとほかの車に迷惑をかけるので、合図をしたらすぐにハンドルを切ることが最も安全な方法である。
questions.explanation: False. For a course change, the signal is normally given about three seconds before the change. The driver must check safety before steering and must not change course immediately merely because the signal has been activated.

questions.question_en: When starting from a parked position, give the starting signal, check the right rear and the surrounding area, and start in a way that does not interfere with other traffic.
questions.question_ja: 駐車している車を発進させるときは、発進の合図を出すとともに、右後方及び周囲の安全を確認し、ほかの交通に迷惑を及ぼさないように発進する。
questions.explanation: True. Moving out from a parked position requires both a signal and a safety check, especially to the right and rear where traffic may be approaching.

questions.question_en: When overtaking, it is temporarily permitted to exceed the maximum speed established by law or by signs.
questions.question_ja: 追越すためであれば、法令や標識で定められた最高速度を一時的にこえることは許される。
questions.explanation: False. The maximum speed limit still applies during overtaking; overtaking does not create an exception to the speed limit.

questions.question_en: At an uncontrolled intersection with poor visibility like this, a vehicle reaching point A may pass before a vehicle coming from direction B, so it does not need to slow down.
questions.question_ja: このような見通しのよくない信号のない交差点では、A地点に差しかかった車は、B方向からの車より先に通ることができるので、徐行しなくてもよい。
questions.explanation: False. At a poorly visible uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle must slow down as required; any priority relationship does not remove the duty to approach cautiously.

questions.question_en: When turning right or left, excluding a roundabout, the signal must be continued until the turn is completed.
questions.question_ja: 右折や左折などをするとき（環状交差点を除く）は、その行為が終わるまで、合図を継続しなければならない。
questions.explanation: True. A turn signal must remain on from the required starting point until the turning maneuver has finished.

questions.question_en: When a signal is marked 'Pedestrians/Bicycles Only,' pedestrians, ordinary bicycles, and motorized bicycles must all obey that signal.
questions.question_ja: このように信号に「歩行者・自転車専用」と表示されている場合は、歩行者と普通自転車と原動機付自転車は、この信号機の信号に従わなければならない。
questions.explanation: False. The pedestrian/bicycle signal applies to pedestrians and bicycles and, under current rules, specified small motorized bicycles in the applicable cases; an ordinary motorized bicycle is not included simply because the sign says pedestrians/bicycles only.

questions.question_en: Correct use of a child restraint can greatly reduce injuries in a traffic accident and can also prevent a child from interfering with the driver's operation of the vehicle.
questions.question_ja: チャイルドシートを正しく使用することにより、交通事故にあった場合の被害を大幅に軽減するとともに、こどもが運転操作の支障となることを防止する。
questions.explanation: True. A correctly fitted child restraint protects the child in a collision and helps keep the child from moving into a position that interferes with driving controls.
